504	**D.9 Dirty-key collapse**
505	
506	The `change_keys` formula is defined as:
507	
508	`change_keys(b, T) = dirty(b, T) if |dirty(b, T)| ≤ MAX_DIRTY_KEYS else ALL`
509	
510	**Variables:**
511	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
512	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
513	| dirty(b, T) | set of key | 0–|keys(b)| | calculated (explicit marks in mutators — CR-8's packed-array gotcha) | Keys of block `b` written during P2/P3 of tick `T` |
514	| MAX_DIRTY_KEYS | int | 32–4096 (default **256**; never below 128 while the Graph is registered, Graph D.10) | data file | Collapse threshold |
515	| change_keys | set of key ∪ {ALL} | — | calculated | Delivered in P5 as `(block_id, T, change_keys)` |
516	
517	**Output Range:** A set of at most 256 keys, or the sentinel `ALL`. Collapse is worth it when `|dirty| × c_key > c_full` — the per-key subscriber refresh cost times count exceeds a full-block refresh — so the threshold should sit near `c_full / c_key`; the Graph (largest key volume) sets it, per Interactions row 1. A block with no dirty keys emits nothing. Notification payload is therefore bounded at `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS × key_size` per block per tick.
518	**Example:** A weld dirties 14 Graph keys → delivered as 14 keys; a hull breach cascading through 300 nodes → `ALL`; Failure & Trail does one full re-read.
519	
520	**D.10 RNG stream derivation**
521	
522	The `rng_derive` formula is defined as: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: GDScript `int` is signed 64-bit and `>>` is an arithmetic shift, so every shift is a masked logical shift and every constant is written signed)*
523	
524	`rng_derive(world_seed, stream_name, counter) = mix64( world_seed ⊕ mix64(fnv64(stream_name)) ⊕ (counter × GOLDEN) )`; `unit = lsr(rng_derive, 11) / 2^53`; `rng_int(lo, hi) = lo + floor(unit × (hi − lo + 1))`
525	
526	with `lsr(x, n) = (x >> n) & ((1 << (64 − n)) − 1)` for 1 ≤ n ≤ 63 (logical shift); `mix64(z)` = the SplitMix64 finaliser: `z = (z ⊕ lsr(z, 30)) × C1; z = (z ⊕ lsr(z, 27)) × C2; return z ⊕ lsr(z, 31)`; `fnv64` = FNV-1a over the UTF-8 bytes of the name, `h = FNV_OFFSET; for each byte: h = (h ⊕ byte) × FNV_PRIME`, **computed once per stream at registration and cached, never per draw**. Constants as GDScript `int` literals (hex shown for reference only — a hex literal above `0x7FFF…` is not a valid `int` literal): `GOLDEN` = 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 = `-7046029254386353131`; `C1` = 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9 = `-4658895280553007687`; `C2` = 0x94D049BB133111EB = `-7723592293110705685`; `FNV_OFFSET` = 0xCBF29CE484222325 = `-3750763034362895579`; `FNV_PRIME` = 0x100000001B3 = `1099511628211`. **Integer wrap on multiplication is intended** and relied on; the golden vectors below (several have the top bit set) fail at once on an implementation that does not wrap or that uses an arithmetic shift.
527	
528	**Variables:**
529	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
530	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
531	| world_seed | int (64-bit pattern) | any `int` | data file (kernel.clock block; set at new game, persisted) | Per-world seed; stored as the signed `int` with the same bit pattern as the u64 |
532	| stream_name | string | registered, e.g. `horror.tell` | data file (owner declares) | Names an independent stream |
533	| counter | int | 0–2^63−1 | calculated (lives in the owner's block, incremented per draw, persisted with it) | Draw index |
534	| mix64 | fn | bijective 64-bit → 64-bit, full avalanche | constant (SplitMix64 finaliser; **set-once**, ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling, R-17 — the kernel ADR may change it only before the first save format ships) | Mixing function |
535	| rng_derive | int (64-bit pattern) | any `int` | calculated | Deterministic raw value (print as `hex64`) |
536	| unit | float | [0, 1) | calculated | 53-bit uniform |
537	| rng_int | int | [lo, hi] | calculated | Uniform integer in an inclusive range; **requires `lo ≤ hi` and `hi − lo + 1 ≤ 2^32`** |
538	
539	**Output Range:** `unit` is in `[0, 1)` exactly (the top 53 bits divided by 2^53 can never reach 1). `rng_int` is inclusive at both ends; its bias is at most `span / 2^53 ≤ 2^-21` (there is no modulo, so no modulo bias, and the span cap is what keeps it negligible). A call with `lo > hi` or a span above 2^32 is a caller defect: it returns `lo`, increments `RNG_RANGE_VIOLATION` and reports a violation (CR-19). Pure: the same `(seed, name, counter)` always gives the same value regardless of call order or which other streams drew — which is what lets G3 replay and G4 save-equivalence hold with no RNG state outside blocks. A stream's counter restores with its block, so a save mid-tell reproduces the same tell.
540	**Golden vectors** (computed with an independent 64-bit reference implementation; these are the acceptance values): `fnv64("horror.tell")` = `0xE500B5B58A7689E2`; `mix64(1)` = `0x5692161D100B05E5`; `mix64(0x8000000000000000)` = `0x25C26EA579CEA98A`; with `world_seed = 0x5EED000000002026`: `rng_derive(seed, "horror.tell", 17)` = `0xB2AA94991B52A02E` → `unit ≈ 0.6979153513` → `rng_int(600, 1800) = 600 + floor(0.6979153513 × 1201) = 600 + 838 = 1438` ticks ≈ 24.0 s; `rng_derive(seed, "horror.tell", 0)` = `0x4988DBEFD7F20FF5`; `rng_derive(seed, "graph.failure", 0)` = `0x0CEEC43F97221B55`; with `world_seed = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`: `rng_derive(seed, "horror.tell", 1)` = `0x883EA97FED4A4613`. The `horror.tell` / `rng_int(600, 1800)` usage matches Horror's HE-9 stream use (*Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from horror-entities*).
541	
542	*Maintenance note:* a 63-bit owner-defined key (for example the Graph's `(step_no, subject_id)`) is a valid `counter` for `rng_derive` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (SL-23))*.
543	
544	**Restore-epoch re-keying** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1; implements user ruling X8/D16, which stands unchanged)*. The one place a restore epoch enters a draw is a kernel helper; Attention and Horror call it and define no derivation of their own:
545	
546	`rng_derive_epoch(world_seed, stream_name, rng_counter) = rng_derive( world_seed, stream_name, counter_eff )`, `counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE × restore_epoch`
547	
548	**Variables:**
549	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
550	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
551	| rng_counter | int | 0 to `RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE − 1` | calculated (lives in the threat owner's `WORLD` block, persisted) | The owner's own stream position; restores exactly and is never rerolled by a restore |
552	| restore_epoch | int (u32) | 0 to 2^32 − 1 | Save/Load (persisted in the per-slot side file `slot_epoch.bin`, SL-23); the kernel exposes it read-only in the `kernel.clock` read view | Advances by 1 on a death-stub restore, a `FAULT_RECOVERY` and a Continue of any generation other than the newest non-demoted verified `QUIT` generation (in-process or after a fresh process start), so two death restores of one autosave install e + 1 and e + 2; a Continue of that `QUIT` generation carries it unchanged. Save/Load's ACs (AC-SL-142, AC-SL-145) own the advance, carry and durability halves *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14)* |
553	| RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE | int | fixed 1,048,576 (2^20) | constant (the kernel owns it; value unchanged from the Attention GDD's figure) | Keeps the epoch term from colliding with any reachable `rng_counter` |
554	| counter_eff | int | 0 to 2^52 − 1 | calculated | The counter handed to `rng_derive`; below 2^63, so D.10's counter range holds |
555	
556	**Output Range / guards (G5):** `stream_name` hash stays cached and unchanged (only `counter` moves). Preconditions: `0 ≤ rng_counter < RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE` and `0 ≤ restore_epoch ≤ 2^32 − 1`. A call that breaks either is a caller defect: `RNG_COUNTER_RANGE_VIOLATION` increments, a violation is reported (CR-19), and the value is still computed as written (deterministic, never a trap); a `request_restore` carrying an epoch outside the u32 range fails its pre-check `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE` → `FAULTED` (the same path as `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH`). At `restore_epoch = 0` the helper equals plain `rng_derive`. **Scope**: threat draws only (Attention's `attention.tell`, Horror's REACH-length draw). Graph physical failures and every persisted counter call plain `rng_derive` and never read the epoch, so they replay exactly. **Accurate behaviour (replacing the earlier claim that quitting or dying could not move a draw, which was wrong in both directions while the epoch reset on process start)**: every advancing restore (a death-stub restore, a `FAULT_RECOVERY`, a Continue of any generation other than the newest `QUIT` one) yields a new epoch, so a threat draw made after it is never a repeat of the one the earlier run met; a Save & Quit then Continue carries the epoch, so the draws after it are exactly those an uninterrupted run would make, and quitting buys nothing (user ruling D16, delegated ruling R13). The one listed exposure is R14's failure path: if Save/Load's `slot_epoch.bin` write fails or times out, a kill before its next successful write may replay that epoch once (CR-15) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14)*; determinism (G3/G4) is defined given the pair `(save bytes, restore_epoch)`: the same pair replays identically, and tests pin the epoch.
557	**Example (golden, `world_seed = 0x5EED000000002026`, stream `"horror.tell"`, `rng_counter = 17`):** epoch 0 → `counter_eff = 17` → `0xB2AA94991B52A02E` (`rng_int(600, 1800) = 1438`, the existing vector); epoch 1 → `counter_eff = 1,048,593` → `0x6EFE2D9E722654C6` (`unit ≈ 0.4335659515` → 1120); epoch 2 → `counter_eff = 2,097,169` → `0xA46E009E591F2390` (`unit ≈ 0.6423035037` → 1371). The three differ, as AC KRN-EPO-01 requires.
558	
559	**D.11 Snapshot size and capture budget**
560	
561	The `snapshot_bytes` formula is defined as:
562	
563	`snapshot_bytes = header_bytes + Σ_{b ∈ persist} (block_header_bytes + canonical_bytes(b))`
564	
565	**Variables:**
566	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
567	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
568	| header_bytes | int | ~64 | calculated | `T`, `world_seed`, `TICK_RATE` (ratified 2026-10-27, R-9), block count |
569	| block_header_bytes | int | ~48 | calculated | `block_id`, `schema_version`, byte length |
570	| canonical_bytes(b) | int | 0–unbounded | calculated (owner's `snapshot()`, then the canonical encoder) | Size of the block's canonical form; `Packed*Array` fields are their raw bytes, so the large Graph arrays cost a memcpy, not a GDScript loop *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
571	| persist | set | ≤ MAX_BLOCKS (**128** registry cap; **32** expected) | data file | Blocks with `persist = true` |
572	| snapshot_bytes | int | — | calculated | In-memory snapshot size handed to Save/Load |
573	
574	**Output Range:** Unbounded in principle; Save/Load owns the on-disk form. Expectation for MVP: ≈ 100–300 KiB, dominated by the Graph. *(Provisional until spike.)*
575	**Example:** Graph 2,000 nodes × 6 fields × 8 B ≈ 96 KiB; 31 other blocks at ~2 KiB ≈ 62 KiB; headers ≈ 1.6 KiB → ≈ 160 KiB.
576	
577	The `capture_time_ms` formula is defined as: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the cost is dominated by the GDScript canonical encoder, not the hash function)*
578	
579	`capture_time_ms = Σ_{b ∈ persist} ( t_snapshot(b) + t_encode(b) ) + t_hash`; budget `capture_time_ms ≤ SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS`; per-block guideline `t_snapshot(b) + t_encode(b) ≤ SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS / |persist|`
580	
581	**Variables:**
582	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
583	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
584	| t_snapshot(b) | float | ms | calculated (diagnostics timer) | Owner's `snapshot()` wall time, including its deep copy |
585	| t_encode(b) | float | ms | calculated (diagnostics timer) | The GDScript canonical encoder over the block's Dictionary/Array/scalar fields — budgeted separately because it, not hashing, is the dominant cost; Packed arrays bypass it |
586	| t_hash | float | ms | calculated | `HashingContext` over the canonical bytes the capture has just produced, for every `persist` block (so it never reads the per-block cache and a missed dirty mark cannot leak into a saved hash), plus the fold (D.12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **Runs in release builds too** (K-4 verification window and the Save/Load integrity path), not only in debug/test |
587	| SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS | float | 8–33 (default **16.7** = one 60 fps frame) | data file | CR-18 "cheap" target; the visible hitch at autosave |
588	| capture_time_ms | float | — | calculated | Length of the `SAVING` state in wall time |
589	
590	**Output Range:** The budget is a diagnostics threshold like `STEP_BUDGET_MS`, not a cap — a snapshot is never truncated. Per-block guideline ≈ `16.7 / 32 ≈ 0.5 ms`. GDScript builds Dictionaries at roughly 0.5–1 M entries/s (unverified, spike), so a 0.5 ms block has a budget of ~250–500 scalar fields; any block larger than that must snapshot as `Packed*Array` copies (memcpy-speed), which is the Graph's design constraint. VS-B reuses this as the guest's initial transfer, so the same budget applies there. *(All numbers provisional until spike.)*
591	**Example:** 31 small blocks at 0.1 ms (snapshot + encode) + Graph at 3 ms (packed arrays) + hash 1.0 ms (the freshly encoded bytes hashed once, no cache) ≈ 7.1 ms → under budget; the same Graph as nested Dictionaries at ~25 ms → over, logged.
592	
593	**D.12 State hash (G3/G4)**
594	
595	The `state_hash` formula is defined as: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: two-level hash with per-block cached hashes and length prefixes; scopes made exact)*
596	
597	`block_hash(b) = H64( canonical_bytes(b) )` — **cached per block and invalidated by the block's dirty bit** (any write in P2/P3 clears it; `restore` clears it) **for the diagnostics cadence only**: `state_hash(scope, T, uncached = false)` may use the cache; `state_hash(scope, T, uncached = true)` re-encodes every block in scope and ignores it. **Every determinism check — G3, G4, the K-4 verification window (CR-15), the `STRICT_DEBUG` tripwire and the test profile — calls `uncached = true`**, because in 4.7 a packed-array element write skips the setter, so a mutator that forgets `mark_dirty` leaves a stale cached hash and a cached comparison would pass falsely on exactly the bug G4 exists to catch *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
598	
599	**Published read `block_hash(block_id: StringName, uncached: bool = true) -> BlockHashResult`** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, request from the Layout re-review)*: available in every build — it is not part of the dev-only `diagnostics` accessor (UI Requirements) — it returns `{ok, hash, reason}`, where `hash` is D.12's `block_hash(b)` for one registered `persist` block as the signed 64-bit pattern of `H64` (print with `hex64`). It is a pure read: the kernel calls the owner's `snapshot(ctx)` with a fresh `ctx` of its own (a deep copy that mutates nothing, CR-8, ending `return ctx.complete()`, CR-19), passes the payload through `canonical_encode` and hashes the bytes. With `uncached = true` it ignores the dirty-bit cache and counts as one `canonical_bytes` encode in the KRN-PERF-01 counter; `uncached = false` may return the cache (diagnostics only). **When it may be called:** in any phase or boundary service except while a `WriteScope` is open on that block (inside a P2 `apply`, or a mutator chain that writes it, where the block may be half-written between two mutator calls of one command): there it returns `ok = false` with reason `BLOCK_HASH_IN_WRITE`. From P3 onward, in P5 and in a boundary service it is consistent, because hooks run one at a time. A caller memoises on its own mutation counter so the encode runs only after a block mutation, never per tick; Layout's `layout_hash()` reads it, so Layout and Horror's path cache (HE-25) read it from P3 or a boundary, never from inside an `apply`. The value is the one Save/Load stores as `block_state_hash` (SL-16). An unknown `block_id` or a non-`persist` block returns `ok = false` with reason `BLOCK_HASH_UNKNOWN`, never a hash of 0.
600	
601	**Published encoder `canonical_encode(value) -> PackedByteArray`** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, request from Ship Body)*: the TLV form below is the **only** canonical-bytes definition in the project. An owner GDD describes the *shape* of its `snapshot()` payload (keys, value types, row order) and never a byte layout, and no owner ships its own byte writer. The encoder is a pure static helper (no kernel instance needed, not compiled out of release) and is the same function `block_hash` and `state_hash` use, so an owner test can encode a sub-value of its payload (for example Body's `actors` key).
602	
603	`state_hash(scope, T) = H64( T ‖ world_seed ‖ ⨁_{b ∈ scope, sorted by block_id} ( len(block_id) ‖ block_id ‖ schema_version ‖ len(canonical_bytes(b)) ‖ block_hash(b) ) )`, where `canonical_bytes` is the **prefix-free tag-length-value (TLV) form** below *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; the earlier form carried no type tags and no counts, so `[[1],[2,3]]` and `[[1,2],[3]]` collided, an `int` and a `float` with the same bits collided, and `VECTOR2`, `VECTOR2I`, `NIL` and `STRING_NAME` had no encoding)*: every value is **one tag byte followed by a self-delimiting body**, so no encoding is a prefix of another and the map from values to bytes is injective. Tags and bodies — `0x00 NIL` (no body); `0x01 BOOL` (1 byte, 0 or 1); `0x02 INT` (8 bytes, little-endian two's complement); `0x03 FLOAT` (8 bytes, the IEEE-754 bit pattern, little-endian, with `−0.0 → +0.0` and every NaN → `0x7FF8000000000000`); `0x04 STRING` (u64 little-endian UTF-8 byte length, then the bytes) — **a `StringName` is encoded as the `STRING` of its text**, so equal text is equal bytes; `0x05 VECTOR2` (two normalised `FLOAT` bodies, 16 bytes, no inner tags); `0x06 VECTOR2I` (two 8-byte little-endian ints, sign-extended, 16 bytes); `0x07 ARRAY` (u64 element **count**, then that many tagged values, in order); `0x08 DICT` (u64 entry **count**, then `key, value` tagged pairs sorted bytewise by the **encoded key bytes**; all keys of one dictionary share one type, CR-4); `0x09 PACKED` (one element-type byte, u64 element count, then the raw little-endian element bytes; a `PackedStringArray` element is a u64 length plus UTF-8, a `PackedVector2Array` element is two 4-byte floats). Owners keep NaN and `−0.0` out of packed float state — mutators normalise, and a test asserts it. **Worked examples (hand-derived, normative for the encoder tests; `u64(n)` is 8 little-endian bytes)**: `INT 1` = `02 u64(1)`; `FLOAT 1.0` = `03 00 00 00 00 00 00 F0 3F`; `[[1],[2,3]]` = `07 u64(2) 07 u64(1) 02 u64(1) 07 u64(2) 02 u64(2) 02 u64(3)`, whereas `[[1,2],[3]]` = `07 u64(2) 07 u64(2) 02 u64(1) 02 u64(2) 07 u64(1) 02 u64(3)` — they differ at the second count, so they cannot collide, and `INT 1` and `FLOAT 1.0` differ at the tag
604	
605	**Variables:**
606	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
607	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
608	| scope | enum | {`PERSIST` (G4), `ALL_SIM` (G3)} | calculated (test chooses) | `PERSIST` = blocks with `persist = true` **and** `persist_scope = WORLD` — never `PROFILE`; `ALL_SIM` = every `SIM` block (`WORLD`, `PROFILE` and non-persisted derived). Both **exclude `kernel.clock`** (its `T` and `world_seed` are the hash prefix, so they are counted once) and **never include `PERCEPTION_OUT`** |
609	| H64 | fn | 64-bit digest | constant (ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling, R-17: the first 8 bytes, little-endian, of SHA-256 computed with Godot's `HashingContext`; native speed, no GDScript byte loop; → ADR) | Hash function |
610	| canonical_bytes | bytes | — | calculated | The TLV form above: identical for equal state regardless of insertion order (Godot `Dictionary` is insertion-ordered, so sorting is mandatory) and injective across types, container boundaries and counts *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
611	| state_hash | int (64-bit pattern) | any | calculated | Shown by the Debug Overlay (print as `hex64`); compared by G3/G4 tests |
612	
613	**Output Range:** Uniform over 64 bits; collision probability 2^−64 per comparison, negligible for tests — a claim that now rests on the encoding being injective (the TLV form above; the earlier untagged form made distinct states encode identically, which no hash width could repair). Equal hashes with unequal state would be a false pass, so G4's test also diffs on mismatch rather than only comparing hashes, and the diff runs over the same uncached TLV bytes. **Golden canonical-byte vectors** beyond the hand-derived examples above (a Dictionary with mixed insertion order, a packed array, a `Vector2` with `−0.0`, a `StringName` against a `String`, and Ship Body's fixture of 2 bodies / 3 actors, whose length Body's arithmetic puts at 518 bytes — a candidate the reference implementation confirms or corrects *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*) are **to be computed with an independent reference implementation and frozen at the kernel spike**, as the golden `state_hash` values are (Gaps). Physics-coupled blocks are excluded from `ALL_SIM` in G3 unless physics observations were recorded (CR-13's stated limit). **Cost:** the hash also runs in release (K-4 at every load; the Overlay's cadence in dev), and its cost is dominated by the GDScript `canonical_bytes` encoder, not by `H64`; the per-block cache (diagnostics cadence only — the capture, K-4 and every test hash uncached) means a diagnostics refresh after a tick that dirtied two blocks re-encodes two blocks, Packed arrays reach `HashingContext` as raw bytes, and the encoder is budgeted separately (`t_encode`, D.11).
614	**Example:** Snapshot at T = 5000, restore, run to 5600 → `state_hash(PERSIST, 5600)`; uninterrupted run to 5600 → the same value on both sides (shown as `hex64`); any difference names the first differing `block_id` and key. (No value is quoted here: the digest depends on the unfrozen `H64` choice.)
615	
616	**D.13 Command log coverage**
617	
618	The `log_coverage_ticks` formula is defined as:
619	
620	`log_coverage_ticks = COMMAND_LOG_CAPACITY / cmds_per_tick_actual` if `cmds_per_tick_actual > 0`, else **unbounded** (reported as "entire session"; the guard against division by zero, G5); worst case `COMMAND_LOG_CAPACITY / MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
621	
622	**Variables:**
623	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
624	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
625	| COMMAND_LOG_CAPACITY | int | 256–8192 (default **1024**) | data file | Ring buffer of commands with results (CR-9, diagnostics and replay tests only) |
626	| cmds_per_tick_actual | float | 0–`MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK` (128 at the default) | calculated | Observed admissions per tick; 0 is legal and means the guard branch above |
627	| log_coverage_ticks | float | ≥ `COMMAND_LOG_CAPACITY / MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK`: 8 at the defaults (1024 / 128), 2 at `COMMAND_LOG_CAPACITY = 256` with the default `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK`, and 0.5 at the knob corner 256 / 512 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier "≥ 8" held only at the defaults)* | calculated | How far back the Debug Overlay's "last-N commands" reaches |
628	
629	**Output Range:** At least 8 ticks (133 ms) at saturation with the defaults; at a realistic 0.1 commands/tick (~6/s: a few intents and a tap) ≈ 10,240 ticks ≈ 2.8 minutes. Log entries store the command plus its result and `tick`, ≤ `MAX_PAYLOAD + ~100 B` each → ≤ ~4.3 MiB.
630	**Example:** `1024 / 0.1 = 10,240` ticks ≈ 171 s.
631	
632	**D.14 Tick counter bound**
633	
634	The `ticks_to_overflow` formula is defined as:
635	
636	`ticks_to_overflow = (2^(bits−1) − 1) / TICK_RATE` seconds
637	
638	**Variables:**

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

504	**D.9 Dirty-key collapse**
505	
506	The `change_keys` formula is defined as:
507	
508	`change_keys(b, T) = dirty(b, T) if |dirty(b, T)| ≤ MAX_DIRTY_KEYS else ALL`
509	
510	**Variables:**
511	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
512	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
513	| dirty(b, T) | set of key | 0–|keys(b)| | calculated (explicit marks in mutators — CR-8's packed-array gotcha) | Keys of block `b` written during P2/P3 of tick `T` |
514	| MAX_DIRTY_KEYS | int | 32–4096 (default **256**; never below 128 while the Graph is registered, Graph D.10) | data file | Collapse threshold |
515	| change_keys | set of key ∪ {ALL} | — | calculated | Delivered in P5 as `(block_id, T, change_keys)` |
516	
517	**Output Range:** A set of at most 256 keys, or the sentinel `ALL`. Collapse is worth it when `|dirty| × c_key > c_full` — the per-key subscriber refresh cost times count exceeds a full-block refresh — so the threshold should sit near `c_full / c_key`; the Graph (largest key volume) sets it, per Interactions row 1. A block with no dirty keys emits nothing. Notification payload is therefore bounded at `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS × key_size` per block per tick.
518	**Example:** A weld dirties 14 Graph keys → delivered as 14 keys; a hull breach cascading through 300 nodes → `ALL`; Failure & Trail does one full re-read.
519	
520	**D.10 RNG stream derivation**
521	
522	The `rng_derive` formula is defined as: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: GDScript `int` is signed 64-bit and `>>` is an arithmetic shift, so every shift is a masked logical shift and every constant is written signed)*
523	
524	`rng_derive(world_seed, stream_name, counter) = mix64( world_seed ⊕ mix64(fnv64(stream_name)) ⊕ (counter × GOLDEN) )`; `unit = lsr(rng_derive, 11) / 2^53`; `rng_int(lo, hi) = lo + floor(unit × (hi − lo + 1))`
525	
526	with `lsr(x, n) = (x >> n) & ((1 << (64 − n)) − 1)` for 1 ≤ n ≤ 63 (logical shift); `mix64(z)` = the SplitMix64 finaliser: `z = (z ⊕ lsr(z, 30)) × C1; z = (z ⊕ lsr(z, 27)) × C2; return z ⊕ lsr(z, 31)`; `fnv64` = FNV-1a over the UTF-8 bytes of the name, `h = FNV_OFFSET; for each byte: h = (h ⊕ byte) × FNV_PRIME`, **computed once per stream at registration and cached, never per draw**. Constants as GDScript `int` literals (hex shown for reference only — a hex literal above `0x7FFF…` is not a valid `int` literal): `GOLDEN` = 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 = `-7046029254386353131`; `C1` = 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9 = `-4658895280553007687`; `C2` = 0x94D049BB133111EB = `-7723592293110705685`; `FNV_OFFSET` = 0xCBF29CE484222325 = `-3750763034362895579`; `FNV_PRIME` = 0x100000001B3 = `1099511628211`. **Integer wrap on multiplication is intended** and relied on; the golden vectors below (several have the top bit set) fail at once on an implementation that does not wrap or that uses an arithmetic shift.
527	
528	**Variables:**
529	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
530	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
531	| world_seed | int (64-bit pattern) | any `int` | data file (kernel.clock block; set at new game, persisted) | Per-world seed; stored as the signed `int` with the same bit pattern as the u64 |
532	| stream_name | string | registered, e.g. `horror.tell` | data file (owner declares) | Names an independent stream |
533	| counter | int | 0–2^63−1 | calculated (lives in the owner's block, incremented per draw, persisted with it) | Draw index |
534	| mix64 | fn | bijective 64-bit → 64-bit, full avalanche | constant (SplitMix64 finaliser; **set-once**, ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling, R-17 — the kernel ADR may change it only before the first save format ships) | Mixing function |
535	| rng_derive | int (64-bit pattern) | any `int` | calculated | Deterministic raw value (print as `hex64`) |
536	| unit | float | [0, 1) | calculated | 53-bit uniform |
537	| rng_int | int | [lo, hi] | calculated | Uniform integer in an inclusive range; **requires `lo ≤ hi` and `hi − lo + 1 ≤ 2^32`** |
538	
539	**Output Range:** `unit` is in `[0, 1)` exactly (the top 53 bits divided by 2^53 can never reach 1). `rng_int` is inclusive at both ends; its bias is at most `span / 2^53 ≤ 2^-21` (there is no modulo, so no modulo bias, and the span cap is what keeps it negligible). A call with `lo > hi` or a span above 2^32 is a caller defect: it returns `lo`, increments `RNG_RANGE_VIOLATION` and reports a violation (CR-19). Pure: the same `(seed, name, counter)` always gives the same value regardless of call order or which other streams drew — which is what lets G3 replay and G4 save-equivalence hold with no RNG state outside blocks. A stream's counter restores with its block, so a save mid-tell reproduces the same tell.
540	**Golden vectors** (computed with an independent 64-bit reference implementation; these are the acceptance values): `fnv64("horror.tell")` = `0xE500B5B58A7689E2`; `mix64(1)` = `0x5692161D100B05E5`; `mix64(0x8000000000000000)` = `0x25C26EA579CEA98A`; with `world_seed = 0x5EED000000002026`: `rng_derive(seed, "horror.tell", 17)` = `0xB2AA94991B52A02E` → `unit ≈ 0.6979153513` → `rng_int(600, 1800) = 600 + floor(0.6979153513 × 1201) = 600 + 838 = 1438` ticks ≈ 24.0 s; `rng_derive(seed, "horror.tell", 0)` = `0x4988DBEFD7F20FF5`; `rng_derive(seed, "graph.failure", 0)` = `0x0CEEC43F97221B55`; with `world_seed = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`: `rng_derive(seed, "horror.tell", 1)` = `0x883EA97FED4A4613`. The `horror.tell` / `rng_int(600, 1800)` usage matches Horror's HE-9 stream use (*Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from horror-entities*).
541	
542	*Maintenance note:* a 63-bit owner-defined key (for example the Graph's `(step_no, subject_id)`) is a valid `counter` for `rng_derive` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (SL-23))*.
543	
544	**Restore-epoch re-keying** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1; implements user ruling X8/D16, which stands unchanged)*. The one place a restore epoch enters a draw is a kernel helper; Attention and Horror call it and define no derivation of their own:
545	
546	`rng_derive_epoch(world_seed, stream_name, rng_counter) = rng_derive( world_seed, stream_name, counter_eff )`, `counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE × restore_epoch`
547	
548	**Variables:**
549	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
550	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
551	| rng_counter | int | 0 to `RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE − 1` | calculated (lives in the threat owner's `WORLD` block, persisted) | The owner's own stream position; restores exactly and is never rerolled by a restore |
552	| restore_epoch | int (u32) | 0 to 2^32 − 1 | Save/Load (persisted in the per-slot side file `slot_epoch.bin`, SL-23); the kernel exposes it read-only in the `kernel.clock` read view | Advances by 1 on a death-stub restore, a `FAULT_RECOVERY` and a Continue of any generation other than the newest non-demoted verified `QUIT` generation (in-process or after a fresh process start), so two death restores of one autosave install e + 1 and e + 2; a Continue of that `QUIT` generation carries it unchanged. Save/Load's ACs (AC-SL-142, AC-SL-145) own the advance, carry and durability halves *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14)* |
553	| RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE | int | fixed 1,048,576 (2^20) | constant (the kernel owns it; value unchanged from the Attention GDD's figure) | Keeps the epoch term from colliding with any reachable `rng_counter` |
554	| counter_eff | int | 0 to 2^52 − 1 | calculated | The counter handed to `rng_derive`; below 2^63, so D.10's counter range holds |
555	
556	**Output Range / guards (G5):** `stream_name` hash stays cached and unchanged (only `counter` moves). Preconditions: `0 ≤ rng_counter < RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE` and `0 ≤ restore_epoch ≤ 2^32 − 1`. A call that breaks either is a caller defect: `RNG_COUNTER_RANGE_VIOLATION` increments, a violation is reported (CR-19), and the value is still computed as written (deterministic, never a trap); a `request_restore` carrying an epoch outside the u32 range fails its pre-check `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE` → `FAULTED` (the same path as `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH`). At `restore_epoch = 0` the helper equals plain `rng_derive`. **Scope**: threat draws only (Attention's `attention.tell`, Horror's REACH-length draw). Graph physical failures and every persisted counter call plain `rng_derive` and never read the epoch, so they replay exactly. **Accurate behaviour (replacing the earlier claim that quitting or dying could not move a draw, which was wrong in both directions while the epoch reset on process start)**: every advancing restore (a death-stub restore, a `FAULT_RECOVERY`, a Continue of any generation other than the newest `QUIT` one) yields a new epoch, so a threat draw made after it is never a repeat of the one the earlier run met; a Save & Quit then Continue carries the epoch, so the draws after it are exactly those an uninterrupted run would make, and quitting buys nothing (user ruling D16, delegated ruling R13). The one listed exposure is R14's failure path: if Save/Load's `slot_epoch.bin` write fails or times out, a kill before its next successful write may replay that epoch once (CR-15) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14)*; determinism (G3/G4) is defined given the pair `(save bytes, restore_epoch)`: the same pair replays identically, and tests pin the epoch.
557	**Example (golden, `world_seed = 0x5EED000000002026`, stream `"horror.tell"`, `rng_counter = 17`):** epoch 0 → `counter_eff = 17` → `0xB2AA94991B52A02E` (`rng_int(600, 1800) = 1438`, the existing vector); epoch 1 → `counter_eff = 1,048,593` → `0x6EFE2D9E722654C6` (`unit ≈ 0.4335659515` → 1120); epoch 2 → `counter_eff = 2,097,169` → `0xA46E009E591F2390` (`unit ≈ 0.6423035037` → 1371). The three differ, as AC KRN-EPO-01 requires.
558	
559	**D.11 Snapshot size and capture budget**
560	
561	The `snapshot_bytes` formula is defined as:
562	
563	`snapshot_bytes = header_bytes + Σ_{b ∈ persist} (block_header_bytes + canonical_bytes(b))`
564	
565	**Variables:**
566	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
567	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
568	| header_bytes | int | ~64 | calculated | `T`, `world_seed`, `TICK_RATE` (ratified 2026-10-27, R-9), block count |
569	| block_header_bytes | int | ~48 | calculated | `block_id`, `schema_version`, byte length |
570	| canonical_bytes(b) | int | 0–unbounded | calculated (owner's `snapshot()`, then the canonical encoder) | Size of the block's canonical form; `Packed*Array` fields are their raw bytes, so the large Graph arrays cost a memcpy, not a GDScript loop *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
571	| persist | set | ≤ MAX_BLOCKS (**128** registry cap; **32** expected) | data file | Blocks with `persist = true` |
572	| snapshot_bytes | int | — | calculated | In-memory snapshot size handed to Save/Load |
573	
574	**Output Range:** Unbounded in principle; Save/Load owns the on-disk form. Expectation for MVP: ≈ 100–300 KiB, dominated by the Graph. *(Provisional until spike.)*
575	**Example:** Graph 2,000 nodes × 6 fields × 8 B ≈ 96 KiB; 31 other blocks at ~2 KiB ≈ 62 KiB; headers ≈ 1.6 KiB → ≈ 160 KiB.
576	
577	The `capture_time_ms` formula is defined as: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the cost is dominated by the GDScript canonical encoder, not the hash function)*
578	
579	`capture_time_ms = Σ_{b ∈ persist} ( t_snapshot(b) + t_encode(b) ) + t_hash`; budget `capture_time_ms ≤ SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS`; per-block guideline `t_snapshot(b) + t_encode(b) ≤ SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS / |persist|`
580	
581	**Variables:**
582	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
583	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
584	| t_snapshot(b) | float | ms | calculated (diagnostics timer) | Owner's `snapshot()` wall time, including its deep copy |
585	| t_encode(b) | float | ms | calculated (diagnostics timer) | The GDScript canonical encoder over the block's Dictionary/Array/scalar fields — budgeted separately because it, not hashing, is the dominant cost; Packed arrays bypass it |
586	| t_hash | float | ms | calculated | `HashingContext` over the canonical bytes the capture has just produced, for every `persist` block (so it never reads the per-block cache and a missed dirty mark cannot leak into a saved hash), plus the fold (D.12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **Runs in release builds too** (K-4 verification window and the Save/Load integrity path), not only in debug/test |
587	| SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS | float | 8–33 (default **16.7** = one 60 fps frame) | data file | CR-18 "cheap" target; the visible hitch at autosave |
588	| capture_time_ms | float | — | calculated | Length of the `SAVING` state in wall time |
589	
590	**Output Range:** The budget is a diagnostics threshold like `STEP_BUDGET_MS`, not a cap — a snapshot is never truncated. Per-block guideline ≈ `16.7 / 32 ≈ 0.5 ms`. GDScript builds Dictionaries at roughly 0.5–1 M entries/s (unverified, spike), so a 0.5 ms block has a budget of ~250–500 scalar fields; any block larger than that must snapshot as `Packed*Array` copies (memcpy-speed), which is the Graph's design constraint. VS-B reuses this as the guest's initial transfer, so the same budget applies there. *(All numbers provisional until spike.)*
591	**Example:** 31 small blocks at 0.1 ms (snapshot + encode) + Graph at 3 ms (packed arrays) + hash 1.0 ms (the freshly encoded bytes hashed once, no cache) ≈ 7.1 ms → under budget; the same Graph as nested Dictionaries at ~25 ms → over, logged.
592	
593	**D.12 State hash (G3/G4)**
594	
595	The `state_hash` formula is defined as: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: two-level hash with per-block cached hashes and length prefixes; scopes made exact)*
596	
597	`block_hash(b) = H64( canonical_bytes(b) )` — **cached per block and invalidated by the block's dirty bit** (any write in P2/P3 clears it; `restore` clears it) **for the diagnostics cadence only**: `state_hash(scope, T, uncached = false)` may use the cache; `state_hash(scope, T, uncached = true)` re-encodes every block in scope and ignores it. **Every determinism check — G3, G4, the K-4 verification window (CR-15), the `STRICT_DEBUG` tripwire and the test profile — calls `uncached = true`**, because in 4.7 a packed-array element write skips the setter, so a mutator that forgets `mark_dirty` leaves a stale cached hash and a cached comparison would pass falsely on exactly the bug G4 exists to catch *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
598	
599	**Published read `block_hash(block_id: StringName, uncached: bool = true) -> BlockHashResult`** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, request from the Layout re-review)*: available in every build — it is not part of the dev-only `diagnostics` accessor (UI Requirements) — it returns `{ok, hash, reason}`, where `hash` is D.12's `block_hash(b)` for one registered `persist` block as the signed 64-bit pattern of `H64` (print with `hex64`). It is a pure read: the kernel calls the owner's `snapshot(ctx)` with a fresh `ctx` of its own (a deep copy that mutates nothing, CR-8, ending `return ctx.complete()`, CR-19), passes the payload through `canonical_encode` and hashes the bytes. With `uncached = true` it ignores the dirty-bit cache and counts as one `canonical_bytes` encode in the KRN-PERF-01 counter; `uncached = false` may return the cache (diagnostics only). **When it may be called:** in any phase or boundary service except while a `WriteScope` is open on that block (inside a P2 `apply`, or a mutator chain that writes it, where the block may be half-written between two mutator calls of one command): there it returns `ok = false` with reason `BLOCK_HASH_IN_WRITE`. From P3 onward, in P5 and in a boundary service it is consistent, because hooks run one at a time. A caller memoises on its own mutation counter so the encode runs only after a block mutation, never per tick; Layout's `layout_hash()` reads it, so Layout and Horror's path cache (HE-25) read it from P3 or a boundary, never from inside an `apply`. The value is the one Save/Load stores as `block_state_hash` (SL-16). An unknown `block_id` or a non-`persist` block returns `ok = false` with reason `BLOCK_HASH_UNKNOWN`, never a hash of 0.
600	
601	**Published encoder `canonical_encode(value) -> PackedByteArray`** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, request from Ship Body)*: the TLV form below is the **only** canonical-bytes definition in the project. An owner GDD describes the *shape* of its `snapshot()` payload (keys, value types, row order) and never a byte layout, and no owner ships its own byte writer. The encoder is a pure static helper (no kernel instance needed, not compiled out of release) and is the same function `block_hash` and `state_hash` use, so an owner test can encode a sub-value of its payload (for example Body's `actors` key).
602	
603	`state_hash(scope, T) = H64( T ‖ world_seed ‖ ⨁_{b ∈ scope, sorted by block_id} ( len(block_id) ‖ block_id ‖ schema_version ‖ len(canonical_bytes(b)) ‖ block_hash(b) ) )`, where `canonical_bytes` is the **prefix-free tag-length-value (TLV) form** below *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; the earlier form carried no type tags and no counts, so `[[1],[2,3]]` and `[[1,2],[3]]` collided, an `int` and a `float` with the same bits collided, and `VECTOR2`, `VECTOR2I`, `NIL` and `STRING_NAME` had no encoding)*: every value is **one tag byte followed by a self-delimiting body**, so no encoding is a prefix of another and the map from values to bytes is injective. Tags and bodies — `0x00 NIL` (no body); `0x01 BOOL` (1 byte, 0 or 1); `0x02 INT` (8 bytes, little-endian two's complement); `0x03 FLOAT` (8 bytes, the IEEE-754 bit pattern, little-endian, with `−0.0 → +0.0` and every NaN → `0x7FF8000000000000`); `0x04 STRING` (u64 little-endian UTF-8 byte length, then the bytes) — **a `StringName` is encoded as the `STRING` of its text**, so equal text is equal bytes; `0x05 VECTOR2` (two normalised `FLOAT` bodies, 16 bytes, no inner tags); `0x06 VECTOR2I` (two 8-byte little-endian ints, sign-extended, 16 bytes); `0x07 ARRAY` (u64 element **count**, then that many tagged values, in order); `0x08 DICT` (u64 entry **count**, then `key, value` tagged pairs sorted bytewise by the **encoded key bytes**; all keys of one dictionary share one type, CR-4); `0x09 PACKED` (one element-type byte, u64 element count, then the raw little-endian element bytes; a `PackedStringArray` element is a u64 length plus UTF-8, a `PackedVector2Array` element is two 4-byte floats). Owners keep NaN and `−0.0` out of packed float state — mutators normalise, and a test asserts it. **Worked examples (hand-derived, normative for the encoder tests; `u64(n)` is 8 little-endian bytes)**: `INT 1` = `02 u64(1)`; `FLOAT 1.0` = `03 00 00 00 00 00 00 F0 3F`; `[[1],[2,3]]` = `07 u64(2) 07 u64(1) 02 u64(1) 07 u64(2) 02 u64(2) 02 u64(3)`, whereas `[[1,2],[3]]` = `07 u64(2) 07 u64(2) 02 u64(1) 02 u64(2) 07 u64(1) 02 u64(3)` — they differ at the second count, so they cannot collide, and `INT 1` and `FLOAT 1.0` differ at the tag
604	
605	**Variables:**
606	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
607	|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
608	| scope | enum | {`PERSIST` (G4), `ALL_SIM` (G3)} | calculated (test chooses) | `PERSIST` = blocks with `persist = true` **and** `persist_scope = WORLD` — never `PROFILE`; `ALL_SIM` = every `SIM` block (`WORLD`, `PROFILE` and non-persisted derived). Both **exclude `kernel.clock`** (its `T` and `world_seed` are the hash prefix, so they are counted once) and **never include `PERCEPTION_OUT`** |
609	| H64 | fn | 64-bit digest | constant (ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling, R-17: the first 8 bytes, little-endian, of SHA-256 computed with Godot's `HashingContext`; native speed, no GDScript byte loop; → ADR) | Hash function |
610	| canonical_bytes | bytes | — | calculated | The TLV form above: identical for equal state regardless of insertion order (Godot `Dictionary` is insertion-ordered, so sorting is mandatory) and injective across types, container boundaries and counts *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
611	| state_hash | int (64-bit pattern) | any | calculated | Shown by the Debug Overlay (print as `hex64`); compared by G3/G4 tests |
612	
613	**Output Range:** Uniform over 64 bits; collision probability 2^−64 per comparison, negligible for tests — a claim that now rests on the encoding being injective (the TLV form above; the earlier untagged form made distinct states encode identically, which no hash width could repair). Equal hashes with unequal state would be a false pass, so G4's test also diffs on mismatch rather than only comparing hashes, and the diff runs over the same uncached TLV bytes. **Golden canonical-byte vectors** beyond the hand-derived examples above (a Dictionary with mixed insertion order, a packed array, a `Vector2` with `−0.0`, a `StringName` against a `String`, and Ship Body's fixture of 2 bodies / 3 actors, whose length Body's arithmetic puts at 518 bytes — a candidate the reference implementation confirms or corrects *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*) are **to be computed with an independent reference implementation and frozen at the kernel spike**, as the golden `state_hash` values are (Gaps). Physics-coupled blocks are excluded from `ALL_SIM` in G3 unless physics observations were recorded (CR-13's stated limit). **Cost:** the hash also runs in release (K-4 at every load; the Overlay's cadence in dev), and its cost is dominated by the GDScript `canonical_bytes` encoder, not by `H64`; the per-block cache (diagnostics cadence only — the capture, K-4 and every test hash uncached) means a diagnostics refresh after a tick that dirtied two blocks re-encodes two blocks, Packed arrays reach `HashingContext` as raw bytes, and the encoder is budgeted separately (`t_encode`, D.11).
614	**Example:** Snapshot at T = 5000, restore, run to 5600 → `state_hash(PERSIST, 5600)`; uninterrupted run to 5600 → the same value on both sides (shown as `hex64`); any difference names the first differing `block_id` and key. (No value is quoted here: the digest depends on the unfrozen `H64` choice.)
615	
616	**D.13 Command log coverage**
617	
618	The `log_coverage_ticks` formula is defined as:
619

The spec stays parametric in the value. | user, creative-director | Closed 2026-10-27 |

# Godot — Breaking Changes

Last verified: 2026-10-17 (4.6 → 4.7 and the section dates); 2026-02-12 (older sections)

Changes between Godot versions, focused on post-LLM-cutoff changes (4.4+).

## 4.6 → 4.7 (Jun 2026 — POST-CUTOFF, HIGH RISK)

From the official migration guide
(https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.7.html,
checked 2026-10-17). Rows marked **GDScript breaks** stop existing GDScript from
working; the rest add optional parameters, change C# compatibility only, or
change behaviour or defaults. The guide lists no deprecations.

| Subsystem | Change | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| GDScript | Overrides inherit a typed return | An override of a method with a typed return now inherits that type, so it needs an explicit `return` (add `return null` to fix the error). **GDScript breaks** |
| GDScript | Packed array element writes | Setting one element of a packed array no longer calls the setter of the whole packed-array property |
| GUI | `RichTextLabel.ImageUpdateMask.UPDATE_WIDTH_IN_PERCENT` renamed | Now `UPDATE_WIDTH_UNIT`. **GDScript breaks** |
| GUI | `RichTextLabel.add_image()` / `update_image()` | `width` / `height` are `float` (were `int`); `width_in_percent` / `height_in_percent` renamed `width_unit` / `height_unit`, typed `RichTextLabel.ImageUnit` (were `bool`, default `false` → `0`). C# source breaks |
| GUI | `Control.accessibility_live` type | `AccessibilityServer.AccessibilityLiveMode` (was `DisplayServer.AccessibilityLiveMode`). C# breaks |
| Core | `Object.is_class()` | Parameter is `StringName` (was `String`) |
| Core | `OptimizedTranslation.generate()` | Returns `bool` (was `void`). C# binary breaks |
| Input | Mouse and keyboard device IDs | Were `0`; now `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE` and `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD`, because some joypads use `0`. Identify events by type or compare `InputEvent.device` to those constants |
| Physics | Jolt: `WorldBoundaryShape3D` plane sign | The sign of `plane.d` is read the way Godot Physics reads it, so it is flipped compared to 4.6: negate it to keep 4.6 behaviour |
| Physics | Jolt: `SoftBody3D` mass and stiffness | Mass defaults to 1 kg for the whole body (was 1 kg per point); `linear_stiffness` is applied differently. Re-tune `linear_stiffness` and `damping_coefficient` on every `SoftBody3D` |
| Physics | Jolt: `Area3D` and `SoftBody3D` | `Area3D` now reports overlaps with `SoftBody3D`; use collision layers and masks to ignore them |
| Physics | `PhysicsServer2D.body_set_shape_as_one_way_collision()` | Optional `direction` added; `PhysicsServer2DExtension._body_set_shape_as_one_way_collision()` requires it (extensions break) |
| Audio | `AudioStreamPlayer2D` / `AudioStreamPlayer3D` `area_mask` default | Changed from layer `1` to `0` (disabled). An `Area2D`/`Area3D` `audio_bus_override` that relied on the default mask stops working until the mask is set back to layer `1` |
| Audio | `AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.tap_back_pos` | Removed. **GDScript breaks** where it is used |
| Rendering | `CanvasItem` line drawing | No antialiasing feather is added, so lines look thinner; widen lines that relied on the old thickness |
| Rendering | `LinearToSRGB` visual shader node | No longer clamps to `[0.0, 1.0]` under Forward+ and Mobile |
| Rendering | `get_format()` moved | From `ImageTexture` / `PortableCompressedTexture2D` to base class `Texture2D` |
| Rendering | `RenderingServer.particles_request_process_time()` | `time` renamed `process_time`; optional `process_time_residual` added (also on `request_particles_process()` of the four particle nodes) |
| Rendering | Sky reflection roughness layers | `rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/roughness_layers` default `7` → `8` |
| Animation | `Animation.length` | Type metadata `double` (was `float`). C# breaks |
| Animation | `LookAtModifier3D.relative` | Default `false` (was `true`) |
| Animation | `AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D/2D.add_blend_point()` | Optional `name` added |
| Project | Stretch defaults for NEW projects | `display/window/stretch/mode` `canvas_items` (was `disabled`), `display/window/stretch/aspect` `expand` (was `keep`). Existing projects keep their settings |
| Text | `ResourceImporterDynamicFont.hinting` | Default `3` (was `1`) |
| Editor | `EditorSceneFormatImporter` import constants | Moved into the `ImportFlags` enum (`IMPORT_SCENE`, `IMPORT_ANIMATION`, …). C# source breaks |
| Editor | `EditorVCSInterface._commit()` | New `amend` parameter; VCS plugins break |
| Editor | Asset Library replaced by the Asset Store | The editor workspace is now "Asset Store" (release notes: https://godotengine.org/releases/4.7/) |
| XR | `OpenXRExtensionWrapper._on_register_metadata()` | New `interaction_profile_metadata` parameter; extensions break |

## 4.5 → 4.6 (Jan 2026 — POST-CUTOFF, HIGH RISK)

| Subsystem | Change | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| Physics | Jolt is now the DEFAULT 3D physics engine | New projects use Jolt automatically. Existing projects keep their setting. Some HingeJoint3D properties (like `damp`) only work with GodotPhysics. |
| Rendering | Glow processes BEFORE tonemapping | Was after tonemapping. Scenes with glow will look different. Adjust intensity/blend in WorldEnvironment. |
| Rendering | D3D12 default on Windows | Was Vulkan. For better driver compatibility. |
| Rendering | AgX tonemapper new controls | White point and contrast parameters added. |
| Core | Quaternion initializes to identity | Was zero. Unlikely to affect most code but technically breaking. |
| UI | Dual-focus system | Mouse/touch focus now separate from keyboard/gamepad focus. Visual feedback differs by input method. |
| Animation | IK system fully restored | CCDIK, FABRIK, Jacobian IK, Spline IK, TwoBoneIK via SkeletonModifier3D nodes. |
| Editor | New "Modern" theme default | Grayscale replaces blue-tint. Restore: Editor Settings → Interface → Theme → Style: Classic |
| Editor | "Select Mode" keybind changed | New "Select Mode" (v key) prevents accidental transforms. Old mode renamed "Transform Mode" (q key). |
| 2D | TileMapLayer scene tile rotation | Scene tiles can now be rotated like atlas tiles. |
| Localization | CSV plural form support | No longer requires Gettext for plurals. Context columns added. |
| C# | Automatic string extraction | Translation strings auto-extracted from C# code. |
| Plugins | New EditorDock class | Specialized container for plugin docks with layout control. |

## 4.4 → 4.5 (Sep 2025 — POST-CUTOFF, HIGH RISK)

| Subsystem | Change | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| GDScript | Variadic arguments added | Functions can accept `...` arbitrary params — new language feature |
| GDScript | `@abstract` decorator | Abstract classes and methods now enforceable |
| GDScript | Script backtracing | Detailed call stacks available even in Release builds |
| Rendering | Stencil buffer support | New capability for advanced visual effects |
| Rendering | SMAA 1x antialiasing | New post-processing AA option |
| Rendering | Shader Baker | Pre-compiles shaders — reportedly 20x faster startup on some demos |
| Rendering | Bent normal maps, specular occlusion | New material features |
| Accessibility | Screen reader support | Control nodes work with accessibility tools via AccessKit |
| Editor | Live translation preview | Test GUI layouts in different languages in-editor |
| Physics | 3D interpolation rearchitected | Moved from RenderingServer to SceneTree. API unchanged but internals differ. |
| Animation | BoneConstraint3D | New: AimModifier3D, CopyTransformModifier3D, ConvertTransformModifier3D |
| Resources | `duplicate_deep()` added | New explicit method for deep duplication of nested resources |
| Navigation | Dedicated 2D navigation server | No longer a proxy to 3D navigation; smaller export for 2D games |
| UI | FoldableContainer node | New accordion-style container for collapsible UI sections |
| UI | Recursive Control behavior | Disable mouse/focus interactions across entire node hierarchies |
| Platform | visionOS export support | New platform target |
| Platform | SDL3 gamepad driver | Delegated gamepad handling to SDL library |
| Platform | Android 16KB page support | Required for Google Play targeting Android 15+ |

## 4.3 → 4.4 (Mar 2025 — BEFORE CUTOFF, VERIFY)

| Subsystem | Change | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| Core | `FileAccess.store_*` return `bool` | Was `void`. Methods: `store_8`, `store_16`, `store_32`, `store_64`, `store_buffer`, `store_csv_line`, `store_double`, `store_float`, `store_half`, `store_line`, `store_pascal_string`, `store_real`, `store_string`, `store_var` |
| Core | `OS.execute_with_pipe` | Added optional `blocking` parameter |
| Core | `RegEx.compile/create_from_string` | Added optional `show_error` parameter |
| Rendering | `RenderingDevice.draw_list_begin` | Many parameters removed; `breadcrumb` parameter added |
| Rendering | `Shader.set_default_texture_parameter()` / `get_default_texture_parameter()` | Parameter/return type changed from `Texture2D` to `Texture`; the shading language did not change |
| Particles | `.restart()` method | Added optional `keep_seed` parameter (CPU/GPU 2D/3D) |
| GUI | `RichTextLabel.push_meta` | Added optional `tooltip` parameter |
| GUI | `GraphEdit.connect_node` | Added optional `keep_alive` parameter |

## 4.2 → 4.3 (In Training Data — LOW RISK)

| Subsystem | Change | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| Animation | `Skeleton3D.add_bone` returns `int32` | Was `void` |
| Animation | `bone_pose_updated` signal | Replaced by `skeleton_updated` |
| TileMap | `TileMapLayer` replaces `TileMap` | One node per layer instead of multi-layer single node |
| Navigation | `NavigationRegion2D` | Removed `avoidance_layers`, `constrain_avoidance` properties |
| Editor | `EditorSceneFormatImporterFBX` | Renamed to `EditorSceneFormatImporterFBX2GLTF` |
| Animation | AnimationMixer base class | AnimationPlayer and AnimationTree now extend AnimationMixer |

## Sources

- Official docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/
- 4.6→4.7 migration: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.7.html
- 4.5→4.6 migration: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.6.html
- 4.4→4.5 migration: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.5.html
- Changelog: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md
- Release notes: https://godotengine.org/releases/4.7/ (4.6: https://godotengine.org/releases/4.6/)
- Releases and dates: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/releases
# Godot — Deprecated APIs

Last verified: 2026-10-17 (4.7 rows); 2026-02-12 (rest)

The 4.7 migration guide lists no formal deprecations; the 4.7 rows below are
renames and removals from it
(https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.7.html).

If an agent suggests any API in the "Deprecated" column, it MUST be replaced
with the "Use Instead" column.

## Nodes & Classes

| Deprecated | Use Instead | Since | Notes |
|------------|-------------|-------|-------|
| `TileMap` | `TileMapLayer` | 4.3 | One node per layer instead of multi-layer node |
| `VisibilityNotifier2D` | `VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D` | 4.0 | Renamed for clarity |
| `VisibilityNotifier3D` | `VisibleOnScreenNotifier3D` | 4.0 | Renamed for clarity |
| `YSort` | `Node2D.y_sort_enabled` | 4.0 | Property on Node2D, not a separate node |
| `Navigation2D` / `Navigation3D` | `NavigationServer2D` / `NavigationServer3D` | 4.0 | Server-based API |
| `EditorSceneFormatImporterFBX` | `EditorSceneFormatImporterFBX2GLTF` | 4.3 | Renamed |

## Methods & Properties

| Deprecated | Use Instead | Since | Notes |
|------------|-------------|-------|-------|
| `yield()` | `await signal` | 4.0 | GDScript 2.0 coroutine syntax |
| `connect("signal", obj, "method")` | `signal.connect(callable)` | 4.0 | Callable-based connections |
| `instance()` | `instantiate()` | 4.0 | Renamed |
| `PackedScene.instance()` | `PackedScene.instantiate()` | 4.0 | Renamed |
| `get_world()` | `get_world_3d()` | 4.0 | Explicit 2D/3D split |
| `OS.get_ticks_msec()` | `Time.get_ticks_msec()` | 4.0 | Time singleton preferred |
| `duplicate()` for nested resources | `duplicate_deep()` | 4.5 | Explicit deep copy control |
| `Skeleton3D` signal `bone_pose_updated` | `skeleton_updated` | 4.3 | Renamed |
| `AnimationPlayer.method_call_mode` | `AnimationMixer.callback_mode_method` | 4.3 | Moved to base class |
| `AnimationPlayer.playback_active` | `AnimationMixer.active` | 4.3 | Moved to base class |
| `RichTextLabel.ImageUpdateMask.UPDATE_WIDTH_IN_PERCENT` | `ImageUpdateMask.UPDATE_WIDTH_UNIT` | 4.7 | Renamed; GDScript using the old name breaks |
| `add_image()` / `update_image()` `width_in_percent`, `height_in_percent` (`bool`) | `width_unit`, `height_unit` (`RichTextLabel.ImageUnit`) | 4.7 | Renamed and retyped |
| `DisplayServer.AccessibilityLiveMode` for `Control.accessibility_live` | `AccessibilityServer.AccessibilityLiveMode` | 4.7 | Enum moved to `AccessibilityServer` |
| `AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.tap_back_pos` | — | 4.7 | Removed |
| `EditorSceneFormatImporter.IMPORT_*` constants | `EditorSceneFormatImporter.ImportFlags` enum | 4.7 | Same names, now in an enum |

## Patterns (Not Just APIs)

| Deprecated Pattern | Use Instead | Why |
|--------------------|-------------|-----|
| String-based `connect()` | Typed signal connections | Type-safe, refactor-friendly |
| `$NodePath` in `_process()` | `@onready var` cached reference | Performance: path lookup every frame |
| Untyped `Array` / `Dictionary` | `Array[Type]`, typed variables | GDScript compiler optimizations |
| `Texture2D` in `Shader.set_default_texture_parameter()` / `get_default_texture_parameter()` | `Texture` base type | Changed in 4.4; the shading language's `sampler2D` / `texture()` did not change |
| Manual post-process viewport chains | `Compositor` + `CompositorEffect` | Structured post-processing (4.3+) |
| GodotPhysics3D for new projects | Jolt Physics 3D | Default since 4.6; better stability |
| `event.device == 0` to detect mouse or keyboard | `event is InputEventMouse` / `InputEventKey`, or `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE` / `DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD` | Since 4.7 mouse and keyboard no longer report device `0`, which some joypads use |
| Installing addons from the editor's AssetLib tab | The editor's Asset Store workspace (4.7+) | 4.7 replaced the Asset Library with the Asset Store |

# ADR-0007: Static Content Data Pipeline and Stable Type IDs

## Status
Proposed

## Date
2026-10-28

## Last Verified
2026-10-28 (against `design/gdd/item-and-module-database.md` IDB-3, IDB-4, IDB-26, IDB-27, IDB-30; `ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md` LY-2, LY-30; `life-support-graph.md` LS-2 to LS-5 and `GRAPH_BOOT_TYPE_ID`; `derelict-authoring-handmade-kits.md` DA-4, DA-41; `docs/architecture/tr-baseline.md` rows citing ADR-0007; ADR-0003 § 6; and `docs/engine-reference/godot/` `VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md`, `deprecated-apis.md`). No code exists and nothing here has been run on 4.7.2. The pinned engine reference has no core, scripting or export module, so every engine claim about `FileAccess`, `JSON`, `DirAccess` and export filters rests on training knowledge of APIs that predate 4.4 and is spike-bound (CONTENT-EXP-1).

## Decision Makers
Claude (author), running under `modes.automation: autonomous` (`project.yaml`), with every decision point logged in `production/session-logs/decision-log.md` for the user's review; the user has not yet reviewed this ADR. Reviewed by godot-specialist (engine: idiomatic; three blocking detail errors and fifteen minor notes, all applied) and technical-director (TD-ADR: CONCERNS; findings 1 to 12 applied in this revision). See Review Log.

## Summary
Sixty-five requirements from fifteen GDDs need static authored data (items, section templates, world records, tuning tables, lint configuration) to load identically in the editor, headless tests and a release export, to reach the simulation only as integers, and to keep ids stable across saves. This ADR fixes one pipeline: integer-only JSON under `assets/data/` listed in committed manifests (never a directory scan), read through an injected `ContentSource`, parsed with `JSON.new().parse`, cast through closed per-table schemas into write-once typed `RefCounted` catalogs, validated by one flat domain-2 boot-error list plus an offline lint that reuses the same loaders, and keyed by append-only id ledgers that CI diffs against a base revision.

## Engine Compatibility

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (stable), GDScript |
| **Domain** | Core (file I/O, JSON parsing, project export configuration, data-class design) |
| **Knowledge Risk** | LOW for the APIs (`FileAccess.open`, `FileAccess.get_open_error`, `FileAccess.get_as_text`, `JSON.new().parse`, `JSON.get_data` / `get_error_line` / `get_error_message`, `Array.make_read_only` / `is_read_only`, `roundi`, `Performance.get_monitor(OBJECT_COUNT)` all predate 4.4 and are not listed in `breaking-changes.md` for 4.4 to 4.7). MEDIUM confidence overall, because the pinned reference has no core/scripting/export module: JSON number typing, the include-filter glob syntax and the export of `.json` files are training-knowledge claims, bound to spike CONTENT-EXP-1. The 4.7 rows that matter are the typed-return override rule (every `ContentSource` override returns a `ContentRead` on all paths) and the packed-array element-write change (not engaged: catalogs have no setters). |
| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md` (4.4 `FileAccess.store_*` now return `bool`: irrelevant, runtime never writes content; 4.6 to 4.7 GDScript rows), `deprecated-apis.md` (untyped Array/Dictionary pattern row), `current-best-practices.md` (not read for this ADR; its GDScript 4.5 to 4.7 rows are cited through ADR-0003). No module file exists for this domain. |

**3.3 Renames and removals** (IDB-27). The format reserves `renamed_from[]` and `replaced_by` on defs now. Their behaviour is needed only after `SHIPPED`: transitive resolution to `ALIAS_DEPTH_MAX` 8 at restore through `resolve_alias`, and `ITEM_BOOT_ALIAS` on a cycle, a self-alias or an alias equal to a live key. It is implemented in a story that is a **prerequisite of the `SHIPPED` flip**, not in the MVP epic. A removed def that names no `replaced_by` fails restore loudly with the holder's named failure (`GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF` for Graph nodes).

**3.4 Versioning.** `catalogue_version` is a single integer in `meta.json`:
- It is bumped on any def removal, rename or field-shape change.
- It is **not** bumped for a value tuned within its type (F-9).

`VERSION_BUMP_MISSING` compares the catalog's structural signature (keys, field set, removed or renamed defs) with the base revision. It is WARN while the ledger is `PRE_RELEASE` and ERROR after `SHIPPED`. This ADR offers the integer to Save/Load's header, and ADR-0006 places it.

`catalogue_hash` is **diagnostic only and never gates a load**. It is `H64` over the canonical bytes of the post-cast typed rows, sorted ascending by `def_id` (byte order), so a legal renumber never changes it. The encoding and `H64` are ADR-0005's. This ADR fixes the *input*: typed integers after cast, never file bytes, never key order, never float spelling.

**3.5 Template identity and hashes.** `template_id` and `room_key` are stable keys under the `section_templates` ledger. `geometry_hash`, `visual_hash` and `template_hash` are `H64` of the canonical encoding of the post-cast template (ADR-0005). They are computed once at load and never stored in the template file. A template edit between builds is handled by Layout's drift policy (LY-26 e). Changing one authored value by 1 changes `template_hash` and `state_hash` (TR-derelict-007).

### Key Interfaces

```gdscript
class_name ContentLoader extends RefCounted
func _init(source: ContentSource, kernel_tick_rate: int) -> void: ...
func load_all() -> ContentLoadResult: ...      # the only entry; runs stages 1-4 of § 1.7

class_name ContentLoadResult extends RefCounted
var content: ContentSet        # null when errors is non-empty ("set" would clash with Object.set)
var errors: Array[BootError]   # empty on success; all errors of the failing stage
var stage_failed: int          # 0 = none, else 1..4

class_name BootError extends RefCounted
var code: int                  # (2 << 16) | local, ContentFaults
var table: StringName
var key: String
var field: StringName
var line: int                  # JSON line when known, else 0
var detail: String

class_name IntField extends RefCounted
static func read(v: Variant, lo: int, hi: int) -> IntRead   # IntRead { ok, value, code }; boot-only, outside the 25-Object count

class_name LedgerCheck extends RefCounted
static func verify(live_pairs: Array[LedgerPair], ledger: IdLedger) -> Array[BootError]
```

(Each `class_name` above is its own file.) Catalog queries (`def`, `has`, `weight_class`, `repair_part_for`, `compatible_defs`, `defs_of_class`, `salvage_yield`) are specified by the Item DB GDD (IDB-28); this ADR fixes only their shape (§ 1.5).

### Implementation Guidelines

- **Must** load every static table through `ContentLoader` and a `ContentSource`; **must never** call `FileAccess`, `JSON` or `DirAccess` for content anywhere else in `src/`.
- **Must** parse with `JSON.new().parse` and cast every number through `IntField.read` or a declared `SCALED` field; **must never** use `JSON.parse_string` for content, and **must never** let a float from a parse reach a sim field, a hash input or a saved value.
- **Must** read only manifest-listed paths whose case matches the file on disk; **must never** enumerate `res://assets/data/` with `DirAccess` in game code.
- **Must** write tables as arrays of rows sorted by key; **must never** author an id-keyed JSON object or rely on parsed key order.
- **Must** declare schemas as `const` literal rows plus `static func fields()`; **must never** use `static var` in content code.
- **Must** make catalogs write-once, get-only, scene-tree free and constructed with injected inputs; **must never** make a catalog a `Resource`, a `Node`, an autoload or a static singleton.
- **Must** expose arrays as read-only typed `Array[T]` stored once; **must never** return a packed array or a per-call `duplicate()` from a catalog.
- **Must** return `Array[BootError]` from loaders with domain-2 codes from `ContentFaults`; **must never** call `assert`, `push_error` or `quit` in a loader, and **must never** raise a content boot error from an owner's own `*_faults.gd`.
- **Must** list every new data path in its manifest and keep the preset `include_filter` covering `assets/data/*.json`; **must never** add a data file that loads only in the editor.
- **Must** persist `def_id` / `template_id` / `room_key` strings; **must never** persist, hash or replicate an item `type_id` or any position-derived id; **must never** reuse a retired id or key.
- **Must** append to a ledger, never edit or remove a pair; **must** bump `catalogue_version` in the same commit as a structural change.
- **Must** append new codes to the end of `ContentFaults` and its `NAMES`; **must never** renumber a code.
- **Must** keep `src/data/` free of imports from `src/sim/`; **must never** `preload` a sibling system's script.
- **Must** keep generators deterministic and commit their output; **must never** generate content at runtime.
- **Must** feed unit-test fixtures through `MemoryContentSource`; **must never** read `res://assets/data/` from a unit test, except the dedicated shipped-data integration test.

## Alternatives Considered
  - a raw-text shape or duplicate-key violation;
  - a non-append-only ledger change or a missing `catalogue_version` bump after `SHIPPED`;

JSON numbers arrive as `float` (CONTENT-EXP-1 c). `IntField.read(value, lo, hi)` accepts a `TYPE_INT`, or a `TYPE_FLOAT` that is integral (`value == floorf(value)`) and strictly below 2^53 in magnitude (`absf(value) < 9007199254740992.0`); a fractional value or a `TYPE_BOOL` is `CONTENT_FIELD_TYPE`, a magnitude at or above 2^53 is `CONTENT_INT_PRECISION` (the bound is exclusive because `9007199254740993` silently parses to 2^53), outside `lo..hi` is `CONTENT_FIELD_RANGE`. A designer-facing fractional field (a 1.5-tile radius) is declared `SCALED` with a `scale` and converted once by `roundi(x * scale)` (half away from zero, negatives included); the lint `FLOAT_ROUND_AMBIGUOUS` rejects a value whose scaled form lies within 1e-6 of a .5 boundary.
134:**What parsing hides, the raw-text lint sees.** After parsing, `40000.0` and `40000` are the same float, and a duplicate key inside one object has silently kept its last value. So the offline lint scans the raw text of each file and reports `INT_LITERAL_SHAPE` (a `.` or exponent in an integer-typed field, or a literal at or above 2^53) and `JSON_DUP_KEY` (a key repeated inside one object). These are CI ERRORs. At runtime, `1e9` is refused by range and `40000.0` is accepted and converted once.

**LS-9 — Randomness is keyed, never counted.** The only stochastic rules are thaw-burst (C5) and, in VS-A, spark ignition (C9). Each draw is `rng_derive(world_seed, "graph.fail", (step_no << 20) | subject_id)` — the registry form is `mix64(world_seed XOR mix64(fnv64(stream_name)) XOR (counter * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15))` — in GDScript the multiplier is written as the signed int `-7046029254386353131`, because 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 exceeds int64 and S0-b probes how the literal parses *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* with "counter (u64 stored in the owning block)" *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from command-simulation-layer)*; the Graph supplies the key as that counter, so the draw is a pure function of state, order-independent, and unchanged by weld, cut, restore or content added elsewhere. `subject_id < 2^20` is asserted (`MAX_GRAPH_NODES` 4096 and `MAX_GRAPH_EDGES` 8192 fit with room), leaving 43 bits of `step_no`. The clarification that "a stored running counter is one option; any owner-defined 63-bit key is valid" is a **routed amendment to the kernel's D.10**, not this GDD's rule (R4). *Alternative considered:* a sequential counter in the block — rejected (TD R10): a weld adds candidates and the draws of an unrelated derelict change. **Replay is exact and not steerable (user ruling D16 / X8, 2026-10-27)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the Graph's physical failures and persisted counters replay exactly after a restore — a thaw-burst roll is a pure function of `(world_seed, step_no, subject_id)` and the persisted state, the Graph holds no restore-epoch input and reads no epoch (nor `PERCEPTION_OUT`, LS-22), and a reload therefore produces the identical roll, the identical burst or non-burst, at the identical step. Quitting or dying and reloading cannot reroll a Graph outcome. The threat draws of Attention and Horror Entities are re-keyed per restore epoch by their own owners (X8); that is their rule and the Graph neither supplies nor consumes the epoch; the epoch's storage and advance rules (delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13 / R14: a Continue of the newest QUIT generation keeps the epoch, death restores and other Continues advance it, held in Save/Load's per-slot `slot_epoch.bin` and never in a generation file) are Save/Load's and the kernel's, and change no Graph byte *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R13 / R14)*. **The thaw-burst roll window** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the roll window is p
