# ADR-0005: Determinism, Keyed RNG, Canonical Encoding and Hashing

## Status
Proposed

## Date
2026-10-28

## Last Verified
2026-10-28 (against `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md` CR-8, D.10, D.11, D.12 and Acceptance Criteria "Determinism" / KRN-HASH-01..03 / KRN-EPO-01 / KRN-PERF-01..05; `life-support-graph.md` LS-9, LS-21; `save-load-and-versioned-format.md` SL-16, SL-23, F-10; `attention-system.md` AT-8, AT-28; `horror-entities.md` HE-42; `sanity-and-hallucination-rules.md` SN-24; `ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md` LY-33, LY-26 (e); `2d-lighting-and-occlusion.md` LO-19; `emitter-state-and-light-exposure-query.md` AC-2; `suit-and-equipment.md` conventions; `web-map-and-transit.md` WM-37; `docs/architecture/requirements-traceability.md` rows citing ADR-0005 (47 TR-IDs); ADR-0001, ADR-0002, ADR-0003 and ADR-0007 (all Proposed); and `docs/engine-reference/godot/` `VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md`, `deprecated-apis.md`, `current-best-practices.md`). No game code exists. Engine behaviour was probed on 2026-10-28 with the installed `Godot_v4.7.2-stable_mono_win64_console.exe` (a debug editor binary on the developer machine, not a release export), from a scratch directory outside the repository; those results are labelled "probed 2026-10-28". Every other engine claim is UNVERIFIED and names the spike that settles it. The pinned engine reference has no core or scripting module, so it is silent on integer semantics, `HashingContext`, packed-array aliasing and `PackedByteArray` encoding.

## Decision Makers
Claude (author), running under modes.automation: autonomous (project.yaml); decisions logged for the user's review; the user has not yet reviewed this ADR.

## Summary
Twenty-six GDDs promise that the same save bytes plus the same restore epoch and command stream give the same state hash, and each of them re-specified part of the machinery (integer rules, RNG keys, presentation hashes, byte layouts, cached hashes) with conflicting details. This ADR fixes one determinism contract: an integer-only simulation with pinned GDScript integer semantics and a division convention, a stateless `rng_derive` / `rng_derive_epoch` family on SplitMix64 with a facet that makes the threat-draw epoch impossible to get wrong, one prefix-free canonical TLV encoder (dictionary keys sorted by value, packed arrays as raw little-endian bytes) that no owner re-implements, `H64` as the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 over those bytes with a fully specified `state_hash` fold, a kernel-owned per-block hash cache invalidated by `mark_dirty` and never used on a verification path, and one shared pure-integer presentation hash.

## Engine Compatibility

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (stable), GDScript |
| **Domain** | Core (integer semantics, hashing, byte encoding, deterministic ordering) |
| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM. The APIs used (`HashingContext`, `PackedByteArray.encode_s64` / `decode_s64` / `encode_double` / `hex_encode`, `String.to_utf8_buffer`, `Array.sort`, `PackedInt64Array.to_byte_array`, `@warning_ignore*`) all predate 4.4 and none appears in `breaking-changes.md` for 4.4 to 4.7. The reference has no core or scripting module, so integer wrap, shift and division behaviour, packed-array aliasing and hash throughput are not sourced by it; they were probed on the 4.7.2 editor binary (below) and stay unverified on a release export, on Linux / Steam Deck and on macOS until spikes S0-a to S0-d and the cross-OS golden CI job pass. The 4.7 rows that matter are sourced: "Packed array element writes no longer call the property setter" (this ADR's cache invalidation therefore never rides a setter) and "Overrides inherit a typed return" (every `DetRng`, `IntMath`, `CanonicalEncoder` and `Hash64` override returns on all paths). |
| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`; `breaking-changes.md` (4.6 to 4.7 GDScript rows; 4.4 `FileAccess.store_*` row, irrelevant here); `deprecated-apis.md` (untyped Array/Dictionary pattern row; `duplicate()` for nested data replaced by `duplicate_deep()` since 4.5); `current-best-practices.md` (packed-array element-write rule, lines 48 to 52). No module file exists for this domain; none of `modules/*.md` applies. |
| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | `Dictionary.duplicate_deep()` / `Array.duplicate_deep()` (4.5, already required by CR-8 for `snapshot` payloads); `@warning_ignore_start` / `@warning_ignore_restore` (probed 2026-10-28 to compile under 4.7.2 with the `integer_division` warning at error level). No new post-cutoff API is introduced. |
| **Verification Required** | **S0-a (packed-array aliasing and element-write semantics), S0-b (integer semantics), S0-c (literal and shift edge cases) and S0-d (hash throughput)** are the Graph GDD's spikes; the dev-machine results are recorded below and the spikes remain open for a `template_release` export on Windows and Linux/Deck. **Cross-OS golden CI** (TR-lsg-031): the vectors in § 4.6 and § 2.4, and committed golden `state_hash` files for the Graph fixtures, must be equal on Windows, Linux and macOS runners. **S0-e (new): canonical encoder cost** for a 32-block snapshot with a 2,000-node Graph stand-in, a 250-field Dictionary block and a 12-instance holder block, on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK release exports, plus the allocation behaviour of the `PackedByteArray` scratch buffer (`resize`, `slice`). **Ship Body fixture:** the 2-bodies / 3-actors fixture whose length the Body GDD computes as 518 bytes must be encoded by the reference encoder and the length confirmed or corrected (D.12 left it open). **Independent reference:** the vectors below were reproduced by a Python implementation (`hashlib`, explicit masking) in addition to the GDScript probe; the frozen goldens are those the independent implementation produces. |

**Probe record (probed 2026-10-28, `Godot_v4.7.2-stable_mono_win64_console.exe --headless --script`, developer machine, debug editor binary; indicative only, not a release-export measurement).**

| # | Question | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | `int` width and overflow | Signed 64-bit. `9223372036854775807 + 1` is `-9223372036854775808`; `9223372036854775807 * 2` is `-2`. Wrap is silent. |
| P2 | Hex literal above `0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` | The engine reports `Cannot represent 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 as a 64-bit signed integer, since the value is too large` (from `hex_to_int`) when the script is loaded; the value the script then holds was not recorded. The signed decimal constants (`-7046029254386353131` and the others in § 2.1) are mandatory and were used for every vector below. |
| P3 | `>>` | Arithmetic at run time: `-8 >> 1` through variables is `-4`; `(-1) >> 63` is `-1`. **A constant-folded negative shift is a parse error** (`Invalid operands for bit shifting. Only positive operands are supported`, for the literal expression `-8 >> 1`). |
| P4 | Shift counts | Counts wrap modulo 64: `1 << 63` is `-9223372036854775808` and `1 << 64` is `1`. So `lsr(x, 0)` would compute `(x >> 0) & ((1 << 64) - 1)` = `x & 0` = 0 and is invalid; D.10's `1 <= n <= 63` is a real bound. |
| P5 | Division and modulus on negatives | Truncate toward zero; the remainder takes the dividend's sign: `-7 / 2 = -3`, `7 / -2 = -3`, `-7 % 2 = -1`, `7 % -2 = 1`. `posmod(-7, 2) = 1`, `floori(-3.5) = -4`, `roundi(2.5) = 3`, `roundi(-2.5) = -3` (half away from zero). |
| P6 | `integer_division` warning | With `debug/gdscript/warnings/integer_division=2` a bare `a / b` on two `int`s fails to load (`Integer division. Decimal part will be discarded. (Warning treated as error.)`). `@warning_ignore("integer_division")` on the statement and `@warning_ignore_start("integer_division")` / `@warning_ignore_restore("integer_division")` around a function both compile. `debug/gdscript/warnings/directory_rules` exists in 4.7.2 (default `{ "res://addons": 0 }`); the meaning of its values is UNVERIFIED and is ADR-0010's to settle. |
| P7 | Packed-array aliasing | A `PackedInt32Array` is shared by assignment (`var b := a`), by function argument, by a getter that returns the field, and by a Dictionary value read into a local: a write through any alias is visible through the others. `PackedInt32Array.duplicate()` isolates; `Dictionary.duplicate()` (shallow) does **not** isolate a packed array inside it; `Dictionary.duplicate_deep()` does. |
| P8 | Element write and setter | Writing one element of a packed-array property does not call the property setter (the whole-array assignment did, once). This confirms the 4.7 row in `breaking-changes.md`. |
| P9 | `PackedInt32Array` range | A stored value wraps to 32 bits: `3000000000` reads back as `-1294967296`; `& 0xFFFFFFFF` recovers `3000000000`. |
| P10 | Byte layout | `encode_s64`, `encode_u32`, `PackedInt32Array.to_byte_array()`, `PackedInt64Array.to_byte_array()` and `PackedFloat32Array.to_byte_array()` are little-endian. |
| P11 | Float bit patterns | `encode_double(-0.0)` writes the sign bit (`0000000000000080`), and `-0.0 == 0.0` is true. `encode_double` **preserves NaN payloads**: a signalling-NaN pattern `0x7FF0000000000001` and the all-ones pattern both re-encode unchanged, and a `PackedFloat32Array` NaN payload survives `to_byte_array()`. The `NAN` constant encodes as `0x7FF8000000000000`. So normalisation needs explicit branches (`f != f`, `f == 0.0`) and cannot be left to the engine. |
| P12 | String ordering | `Array.sort()` on `String` elements orders by code point, including characters above the BMP (probed `a` 97, `ÿ` 255, `U+FFFF`, `U+1F600` in that order), which equals UTF-8 byte order. `Array.sort()` on `StringName` elements is **not lexical** (`[&"b", &"a", &"c", &"aa", &"B"]` sorted to `[&"c", &"a", &"b", &"B", &"aa"]`). `StringName == String` for equal text is true, and their UTF-8 bytes are equal. |
| P13 | `HashingContext` | `SHA-256("abc")` is `ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad`; `finish()` returns 32 bytes; `decode_s64(0)` of them is `0xEACF018FBF1678BA` (the D.12 value for `H64("abc")`); one `HashingContext` object is reusable by calling `start` again after `finish`. |
| P14 | Throughput (not a release export) | SHA-256 over 4 KB: 0.009 ms; 32 KB: 0.071 ms; 150 KB: 0.332 ms; 300 KB: 0.664 ms. `PackedInt64Array` of 12,000 elements `to_byte_array()`: 0.002 ms. Writing 500 tagged ints with `encode_s64` into a preallocated buffer: 0.020 ms. `DetRng.derive` (three `lsr` calls and two `mix64` calls): 0.48 microseconds per call. A static `floor_div` helper (quotient plus sign fix): 0.37 microseconds per call against 0.016 microseconds for a bare `/` in the same loop. |
| P15 | Vectors | Every D.10 golden vector (`fnv64("horror.tell")`, `mix64(1)`, `mix64(0x8000000000000000)`, the five `rng_derive` values, epoch 1 and epoch 2, `unit` 0.69791535127599 and `rng_int(600, 1800)` = 1438) reproduced exactly on 4.7.2 and in the Python reference. |
| P16 | Hex bytes | `PackedByteArray.hex_encode()` gives lowercase hex of the bytes in order; `String.hex_decode()` **accepts uppercase** and reports an error (empty array) on odd length or a non-hex character, so exact-width and lowercase validation (SL F-10) must be done before decoding. |

## ADR Dependencies

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Depends On** | ADR-0001 (the composition root injects narrow facets; no autoload or global; the kernel clock carries `T`, `world_seed` and `restore_epoch`; Proposed), ADR-0003 (state blocks, `snapshot` callable, `WriteScope.open_for` / `mark_dirty`, fault domains; Proposed). Both must be Accepted before this ADR is Accepted. |
| **Enables** | ADR-0006 (the save container stores `hash_algo`, `state_hash`, `block_state_hash`, `hex64`), ADR-0007 (golden `catalogue_hash` and template hash vectors, § 3.4 / § 3.5 inputs), ADR-0010 (the determinism lint token list and the enforcement split), ADR-0011 and ADR-0012 (Graph data model and propagation: integer headroom, `canonical_bytes` shape, the `(step_no << 20) \| subject_id` key), ADR-0015 (Body integer kinematics), ADR-0016 (restore verification), ADR-0021 (the weld property test uses the hash), ADR-0022 and ADR-0023 (threat draws through `rng_derive_epoch`), ADR-0025 (Sanity streams), ADR-0028 (presentation hash), ADR-0031 (the Overlay's hash display). |
| **Blocks** | Epics: Command & Simulation Layer (hashing, RNG, determinism tests), Life-Support Graph (canonical payload, goldens), Save/Load (hash fields), and every story that registers a state block, draws a random number, divides two possibly negative integers or computes a hash. |
| **Ordering Note** | Written in parallel with ADR-0004, ADR-0006, ADR-0008, ADR-0009 and ADR-0010; every assumption about a sibling is listed under Related and in the author's return value. **Scope edges.** ADR-0003 owns the `snapshot` callable and the descriptor; this ADR owns what the kernel does with the payload (encode, hash, cache). ADR-0004 owns the dirty-key layout and the debug check that every changed block marked a key; this ADR owns the per-block hash-cache invalidation hook that rides the same mark and the hash-side stale-cache detector. ADR-0006 owns the container and what is stored; this ADR owns what is hashed and `hash_algo`. ADR-0007 owns the hash *input* of content (post-cast typed rows); this ADR owns the bytes and `H64`. ADR-0010 owns the lint tool; this ADR owns the rules it enforces. Acceptance also requires S0-a to S0-d on a release export and the cross-OS golden job. |

## Context

### Problem Statement
Determinism is the property that makes replay tests, save verification (K-4), the weld property test, MIRROR comparison and later co-op possible, and it fails silently: one `randf()`, one iteration over an unsorted `Dictionary`, one `-7 / 2` that a designer expected to be `-4`, or one owner writing its own byte layout breaks it with no error. The kernel GDD defines the machinery (D.10 RNG, D.12 hash) and twenty-five other GDDs depend on it, but the GDDs disagree or leave gaps on the details that matter at the byte level:

1. The Graph's `canonical_bytes()` is `[u32 tag][u32 len][bytes]` per field in an owner-chosen order (LS-21), while D.12 says the TLV form is "the only canonical-bytes definition in the project" and no owner ships a byte writer.
2. D.12 sorts dictionary keys "bytewise by the encoded key bytes", which orders integer keys by little-endian two's-complement bytes (3, 10, then -5) and strings length-first. That is deterministic but useless for the diff the G4 test must print (OQ-8).
3. The widths of the `state_hash` fold fields are not stated; `T ‖ world_seed ‖ …` could be hashed with several framings (OQ-8).
4. Attention AT-8 computes `counter_eff` itself and calls `rng_derive`, although the restore-epoch re-keying is "the kernel's one helper" (OQ-6).
5. At least five GDDs define their own pure-integer presentation hash (`he_hash`, Attention `hash32`, Lighting `H(id, k)`, Instruments tremor, Perception Filter D.14) and each marks it "ADR candidate".
6. Integer semantics (division of negatives, shift, wrap, literal range) are marked `[UNV]` in a dozen GDDs and each invents its own guard (Emitter `floor_div`, Suit "non-negative operands only", Web Map "every division takes non-negative operands").
7. `restore_epoch` is "owned by Save/Load" and "exposed read-only in `kernel.clock`" (IC-5), and its exclusion from hashes is stated in several places in different words.

### Constraints
- **Set-once, ratified decisions stand.** `mix64` is the SplitMix64 finaliser (R-17: changeable only before the first save format ships); `H64` is the first 8 bytes, little-endian, of SHA-256 through `HashingContext` (R-17, user ruling X13); `hash_algo` 2 names it (SL-16). D.10's constants and golden vectors are acceptance values.
- **Engine**: Godot 4.7.2, GDScript. `int` is signed 64-bit and wraps; `float` is IEEE-754 binary64; `Dictionary` preserves insertion order; `Array.sort()` is not stable; packed arrays alias by reference. Registry stances in force: no kernel autoload or global (`kernel_autoload_or_global`); blocks are `RefCounted` plain data (`block_as_resource_or_node`); a block is written only inside a `WriteScope` and dirty keys are marked only through `scope.mark_dirty` (`write_outside_writescope_or_setter_dirty`); `var_to_bytes` bytes are never hash input (`payload_size_check`).
- **Budgets** (measured on a release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK, pending spike): a quiet tick performs 0 canonical encodes and 0 kernel container allocations; a read of the hash after a tick that dirtied `k` blocks performs `k` encodes (KRN-PERF-01, -02); a 32-block snapshot captures in at most 16.7 ms including encode and hash (D.11); the P3 budget is 2.0 ms and is unaffected because no hash runs in P3.
- **Hot paths allocate nothing per tick**: nothing in this ADR may allocate in a tick that dirties no block and has no hash reader.
- **No wall clock, no global generator, no scene tree** in anything that feeds a hash (kernel H9, H10).
- Co-op (VS-B) mirrors the host's blocks; the hash definition must be platform-independent in design even though cross-OS identity is verified later.

### Requirements
- One definition of every byte that feeds a hash, shared by all 31 blocks, with no owner-written layout.
- `rng_derive` stays a pure function of `(world_seed, stream_name, counter)`; threat draws re-key per restore epoch through one helper that owners cannot misuse; Graph and every persisted counter never read the epoch.
- Cached per-block hashes for the diagnostics cadence and `layout_hash()` memoisation, and uncached hashes on every verification path, with a debug detector for the stale-cache failure.
- Integer semantics settled once, with a division convention that lints can enforce and a headroom rule that boot assertions can check.
- A replay guarantee stated precisely: what is promised, for which inputs, on which builds and platforms, and what is not.
- Every hash and RNG value that crosses a JSON boundary survives as `hex64` (S-1).

## Decision

### Architecture Diagram

```
 owners (blocks, hooks)            kernel                                      consumers
 ----------------------            ------                                      ---------
 ModuleFacet.rng (RngFacet) --->  RngRegistry  (stream name -> RngStream{key, epoch_keyed}, BOOTING)
   draw(stream, counter)            DetRng.derive(clock.world_seed, key, counter)       pure statics
   draw_epoch(stream, rng_counter)  + clock.restore_epoch (read inside the facet only)
   int_in(raw, lo, hi)              DetRng.int_in  (the one sanctioned float expression)

 owner.snapshot(ctx) --payload-->  CanonicalEncoder.encode(payload)  -->  PackedByteArray (TLV, § 3)
                                            |                                   |
                                            |                      Hash64.of_bytes (HashingContext, SHA-256, first 8 bytes LE)
                                            v                                   v
                                   BlockHashCache {hash, enc_len, valid}   block_hash(id, uncached) -> BlockHashResult
                                      ^  invalidate(block) on scope.mark_dirty / restore / init   (ADR-0004 mark path)
                                      |
                       state_hash(scope, T, uncached) = H64( T || world_seed || fold over blocks sorted by id )  (§ 4)

 pure, stateless, shared:  IntMath (lsr, floor_div, ceil_div, posmod_i, low32)   Ihash (63-bit, presentation and non-RNG variation)   Hex64
 verification:  G3 two-kernel, G4 snapshot/restore/continue, K-4 reproduction compare   all call uncached
```

### 1. The determinism contract: integer-only simulation

**1.1 What is promised.** All promises are about the pair `(save bytes, restore_epoch)`, not the bytes alone, because the epoch re-keys threat draws (D.10).

| Level | Promise | Holds for |
|---|---|---|
| **R1** | Same build, same platform, same `(save bytes, restore_epoch)` and the same ordered command stream plus control-plane request log yield the same `state_hash(scope, N, uncached = true)` at every tick `N`, at any render rate, pause pattern, camera zoom, seat count or MIRROR role. | G3 (two kernels, ALL_SIM), G4 (snapshot, restore, continue, PERSIST), the cross-process test, K-4. |
| **R2** | Same build commit on Windows, Linux x86-64 and macOS: the hashes of the golden fixtures are equal. Expected by construction (integer arithmetic, explicit little-endian bytes, SHA-256, no platform call), **UNVERIFIED** until the cross-OS golden job runs (TR-lsg-031). | The committed `tests/golden/` files. |
| **R3** | Across commits, hashes are comparable only while `hash_algo`, every compared block's `schema_version` and the block payload shapes are unchanged. A deliberate behavioural change moves hashes; goldens are regenerated by an explicit, reviewed job that records the commit. | Golden maintenance. |
| **R4** | A restore with a different `restore_epoch` differs in exactly the threat draws (Attention `attention.tell`, Horror `horror.tell`), nothing else (KRN-EPO-02). | D.10 re-keying. |

**Not promised**: identity across Godot versions (4.7.2 is pinned; a patch upgrade re-runs the goldens), identity of physics-coupled blocks (there is no engine physics in the simulation, so none exist), network timing in VS-B, and anything in `PERCEPTION_OUT` or `PROFILE`-scoped presentation state.

**1.2 Types.** Simulation state is `int`, `bool`, `String` / `StringName` (identifiers, `def_id`), and containers of those, including packed integer and byte arrays. A `float` is not permitted in a persisted SIM block or in any value a SIM rule reads from another block. The sanctioned float expressions are exactly these: (a) `DetRng.unit` and `DetRng.int_in` (§ 2.3), the kernel's one pinned float path; (b) boot-time content casts (`roundi(x * scale)`, ADR-0007), whose results are integers; (c) the driver's `delta_us` conversion (ADR-0001), outside the simulation; (d) test oracles and analysis. Presentation uses floats freely but never writes a sim field and never reads one back through a path a save can see (ADR-0009). A block that must hold a float (none is known at MVP) is added to a committed allow-list, with a one-line reason, and the encoder's strict mode (§ 3.5) then permits it; the allow-list is empty at MVP.

**1.3 Pinned integer semantics** (P1 to P5, P9; recorded in Engine Compatibility). The simulation relies on: 64-bit two's-complement wrap for multiplication in `mix64` and `fnv64` only (intended, and the one place wrap is a feature); arithmetic `>>`; truncating `/` and `%`. It never relies on wrap anywhere else (§ 1.5). Consequences stated as rules:
- Every right shift of a value that can be negative is a masked logical shift: `IntMath.lsr(x, n)` with `1 <= n <= 63`. A bare `>>` is allowed only on an operand proven non-negative (a `& mask` just before, or an unsigned-by-construction value), because `>>` on a negative is arithmetic (P3).
- No shift of a negative **literal** appears in source (P3: a parse error). Constants are written as signed decimal `int` literals; a hexadecimal literal above `0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` never appears (P2). Hex constants in comments are for reference only.
- A shift count is a constant in `1..63` or a variable proven in that range; a count of 64 or more silently wraps (P4).
- A value stored in a `PackedInt32Array` is read back masked when it is meant as unsigned: `IntMath.low32(x)` = `x & 0xFFFFFFFF` (P9). Layout's `geometry_hash` and `visual_hash` (`low32(H64(...))`, LY-26 e) are compared only after this mask (TR-section-032).

**1.4 Division and modulus.** GDScript `/` and `%` truncate toward zero (P5), which is wrong for any quotient a designer meant as a floor. Three rules:
1. **Default: the helpers.** In `src/sim/**` and `src/kernel/**`, division and modulus go through `IntMath.floor_div(a, b)`, `IntMath.ceil_div(a, b)` and `IntMath.posmod_i(a, b)`, all with `b > 0` and correct for either sign of `a` (`floor_div(-7, 2)` is `-4`; `posmod_i(-7, 2)` is `1`; `ceil_div(-7, 2)` is `-3`). `b <= 0` is a caller defect: the helper returns 0 (never aborts: an aborted GDScript function returns a default the caller cannot tell from a result), and the debug-build `assert(b > 0)` fires in tests.
2. **Bare operators on proven non-negative operands only**, and only with the engine's own gate: the statement carries `@warning_ignore("integer_division")` (or sits inside a `@warning_ignore_start` / `_restore` region) **and** a trailing `# nn: <reason>` comment naming why both operands cannot be negative. With `integer_division` at error level (ADR-0010 sets warnings as errors) a bare `/` on two ints cannot compile without that annotation (P6), which makes the escape hatch greppable. A bare `%` has no engine warning, so the lint requires the same `# nn:` marker. The hot-path rationale is measured (P14): the static helper costs about 23 times a bare `/` in a tight loop on the editor binary, so Graph propagation and the Emitter exposure loop may use the marked bare form where the operands are non-negative by construction. S1 (SP-ENG-1) re-measures on a release export.
3. **Fractional designer values are scaled once.** A quantity like 1.5 tiles is stored as an integer in a named unit (ADR-0007 `SCALED` fields); a rule that needs a ratio multiplies first and divides once, on a non-negative numerator (the Emitter wane formula in the Emitter GDD is the model).

The Suit "convention for negative operands" (ADR candidate 4, TR-suit-030) is therefore: floor for every quotient, `floor_div` / `posmod_i`; a thermal integrator that needs truncation toward zero writes `trunc_toward_zero(a, b)` explicitly as `sign(a) * floor_div(abs(a), b)`, and names it. Emitter `floor_div` (non-negative, checked) is a special case of the helper here and Emitter's lint fixtures stay valid.

**1.5 Overflow and headroom.** GDScript `int` wraps silently (P1) and nothing in the simulation detects it at run time. Overflow is designed out, not caught:
- Every sim intermediate stays below `2^62` in magnitude, so a sum of two such values cannot wrap (the Graph and Attention already state this: TR-attention-036, Graph D.13).
- Each owner declares the maxima of its factors as constants; its boot check multiplies declared maxima and fails boot (its own domain's boot code) when a product reaches `2^62` (the Graph's `GRAPH_BOOT_PRODUCT_OVERFLOW` is the model). Tests verify a sample of worst-case inputs against an arbitrary-precision oracle (an offline generator or a test-only big-integer helper; ADR-0010 chooses the tooling).
- The two wrap-intended computations are `mix64` / `fnv64` / `Ihash` (§ 2) and the fold arithmetic in § 4, which use only multiplication and XOR on the full 64 bits and are covered by golden vectors.
- Values that travel through JSON are below `2^53`, or are `hex64` strings (§ 4.8).

**1.6 Ordering.** Anything that feeds a hash, a rebuild, a registration or a result order iterates in an order that does not depend on insertion history, the allocator or the engine version:
- **Dense arrays in ascending id order** is the default container for entities (Layout, Graph, Body). Tombstones stay in place and are part of the array.
- A `Dictionary` is never iterated for order in simulation code unless its keys are first extracted and sorted (`keys()` then `sort()` on all-`int` or all-`String` keys). Insertion order is preserved by the engine but erase-and-reinsert changes it, and a restore rebuilds in file order.
- **`StringName` is never sorted.** `Array.sort()` on `StringName`s is not lexical (P12); convert with `String(k)` first. This is a must-never for canonical ordering and for any sorted iteration.
- `Array.sort_custom` and any sort over keys that can tie are banned in simulation code, because the sort is not stable. A sort that is needed packs the sort key and the stable id into one `int` (`(primary << 20) | id`, with headroom checked) and sorts the `int`s with `Array.sort()`.
- `hash()`, `get_instance_id()`, `ResourceUID`, `shuffle()` and `pick_random()` are banned (engine hash values are not a stable contract; instance ids differ between runs; the other two draw from the global generator).

**1.7 What the lints enforce** (the lint tool is ADR-0010's; this table is the rule set it receives). Where a rule needs more than a regex, the second column says so.

| Rule | Where | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|
| No `randi`, `randf`, `randf_range`, `randi_range`, `randomize`, `seed(`, `rand_from_seed`, `RandomNumberGenerator`, `shuffle`, `pick_random` | `src/sim/**`, `src/kernel/**`, and any presentation file that draws a value a save or a test can observe | regex (allow-list file with a reason per entry) |
| No `Time.`, `OS.get_ticks_*`, `OS.get_unix_time*`, `get_process_delta_time`, `get_physics_process_delta_time`, `Engine.get_frames_*` outside the allow-listed `KernelHost` conversion and render-time timers in Adapter / Presenter (TR-pc-027) | same | regex |
| No `float`, `Vector2(`, `Vector3(`, `sqrt`, `pow(`, `sin`, `cos`, `atan` | `src/sim/**` | regex, except the `DetRng` file and the strict-mode allow-list |
| No `hash(`, `get_instance_id`, `.sort_custom(`, `.shuffle(`, `.pick_random(`, `ResourceUID` | `src/sim/**`, `src/kernel/**` | regex |
| Bare `/` and `%` need the `# nn:` marker (and `@warning_ignore`) | `src/sim/**`, `src/kernel/**` | engine warning plus regex |
| Iterating a `Dictionary` (`for k in d`, `.keys()`, `.values()`) without a sort | `src/sim/**`, `src/kernel/**` | AST or runtime counter (not a regex); fallback: the iterating helper `sorted_keys(d)` is the only allowed form and the regex bans the raw forms |
| `StringName` passed to `sort()` | same | AST (type-aware); fallback: a test that sorts the canonical key set through `CanonicalEncoder` only |
| No owner-written canonical byte writer: no `encode_s64`, `encode_u32`, `encode_double`, `to_byte_array` outside `src/kernel/det/` and tests; no `var_to_bytes` result passed to a hash function | `src/**` | regex |
| No re-derivation of the epoch key (`RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE` appears only in `DetRng` and `RngFacet`) | `src/**` | regex |
| No block declares a float field unless on the allow-list | block payloads | strict-mode encoder in tests (§ 3.5) |

### 2. Keyed RNG

**2.1 The pure family** (D.10, set-once; this ADR restates it so the constants have one home in the ADR set). All functions are stateless statics in `DetRng`. Constants are signed decimal `int` literals (P2); the hexadecimal values are reference only.

| Constant | Signed decimal | Reference hex |
|---|---|---|
| `GOLDEN` | `-7046029254386353131` | `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15` |
| `C1` | `-4658895280553007687` | `0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9` |
| `C2` | `-7723592293110705685` | `0x94D049BB133111EB` |
| `FNV_OFFSET` | `-3750763034362895579` | `0xCBF29CE484222325` |
| `FNV_PRIME` | `1099511628211` | `0x100000001B3` |
| `RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE` | `1048576` | `2^20` |

```
lsr(x, n)      = (x >> n) & ((1 << (64 - n)) - 1)                  1 <= n <= 63
mix64(z)       : z = (z ^ lsr(z, 30)) * C1 ; z = (z ^ lsr(z, 27)) * C2 ; return z ^ lsr(z, 31)
fnv64(name)    : h = FNV_OFFSET ; for each UTF-8 byte b: h = (h ^ b) * FNV_PRIME
stream_key(n)  = mix64(fnv64(n))
derive(seed, key, counter) = mix64(seed ^ key ^ (counter * GOLDEN))      == rng_derive(seed, name, counter) for key = stream_key(name)
unit(raw)      = float(lsr(raw, 11)) / 9007199254740992.0               in [0, 1)
int_in(raw, lo, hi) = lo + floori(unit(raw) * float(hi - lo + 1))        lo <= hi, hi - lo + 1 <= 2^32
```

`mix64` is bijective with the single fixed point `mix64(0) = 0`; this is harmless for `derive` (the stream key is never 0 for a real name) and is why `Ihash` (§ 2.6) demands a non-zero seed or salt.

**2.2 Streams are registered; the key is computed once.** `fnv64` and `mix64` of a name are computed at registration and cached in an `RngStream` object, never per draw (D.10).

```gdscript
class_name RngStream extends RefCounted    # read-only after registration
var name: StringName
var key: int                               # stream_key(name), computed once
var epoch_keyed: bool                      # true for threat streams only (§ 2.4)
```

Owners register streams in `BOOTING` through the facet (§ 2.3). A duplicate name, or two names whose `key` is equal, fails boot with the kernel's `DUPLICATE_ID` fault (ADR-0003 domain 0, code 8) with the stream name in the detail. **Stream names** are lower-case dotted ASCII, `<domain>.<name>` (`horror.tell`, `attention.tell`, `graph.fail`), optionally followed by `/`-separated decimal integers formatted with `str(int)` and no padding (`sanity.lie/3/17`). Names that depend on a runtime id (Sanity's per-seat, per-subject streams, SN-24) are obtained through `facet.dynamic_stream(name, epoch_keyed)`, which memoises the `RngStream` in a bounded cache (`MAX_DYNAMIC_STREAMS` 4096; past it the stream is built without caching and `RNG_STREAM_CACHE_FULL` is counted). The cache is a performance structure only: it is rebuilt on demand, never persisted, never hashed, and its contents are a pure function of the names asked for. The `fnv64` cost per distinct dynamic name is one-time; the string allocation per first use is an accepted cost on a player-driven path (open question 1).

**2.3 The facet owners use.** A module draws only through an injected `RngFacet`, issued by the composition root as `ModuleFacet.rng` (null for a module that declares no streams, which structurally enforces "Web Map registers no `rng_derive` stream", TR-webmap-031, and "Layout draws no RNG", TR-section-026). The facet reads `world_seed` and `restore_epoch` from the kernel clock inside its methods; an owner never passes either, so the epoch cannot be mixed in wrongly.

```gdscript
class_name RngFacet extends RefCounted
func register_stream(name: StringName, epoch_keyed: bool = false) -> RngStream      # BOOTING only
func dynamic_stream(name: String, epoch_keyed: bool = false) -> RngStream            # memoised, bounded
func draw(stream: RngStream, counter: int) -> int          # rng_derive(world_seed, stream, counter); plain streams only
func draw_epoch(stream: RngStream, rng_counter: int) -> int   # rng_derive_epoch; epoch-keyed streams only
func int_in(raw: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int             # rng_int; counts RNG_RANGE_VIOLATION
func unit(raw: int) -> float
```

`draw_epoch` computes `counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE * restore_epoch` and calls `derive`; it is the only code that reads `restore_epoch` for a draw. Violations are counters, not faults (CR-19): `draw` on an epoch-keyed stream and `draw_epoch` on a plain stream count `RNG_STREAM_KIND_VIOLATION`; `rng_counter` outside `0..RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE - 1` or `restore_epoch` outside `0..2^32 - 1` counts `RNG_COUNTER_RANGE_VIOLATION` and the value is still computed as written; `int_in` with `lo > hi` or a span above `2^32` returns `lo` and counts `RNG_RANGE_VIOLATION`; a negative `counter` on a plain stream counts `RNG_COUNTER_RANGE_VIOLATION` and is still computed. Each violation also reports through the CR-19 channel. The `request_restore` pre-check for an out-of-range epoch is ADR-0003's existing `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE` fault (code 6). The pure statics in `DetRng` take explicit arguments and are what unit tests and offline tools call.

**2.4 Epoch re-keying: one place, threat draws only** (resolves OQ-6). `rng_derive_epoch(world_seed, stream, rng_counter) = rng_derive(world_seed, stream, rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE * restore_epoch)`.
- **Epoch-keyed streams at MVP**: `attention.tell` (AT-8) and `horror.tell` (the REACH length, HE-42). Nothing else. A stream is registered `epoch_keyed = true` only with a technical-director ruling; the facet makes the registration visible in one list.
- **Everything else is plain**: the Graph's thaw-burst and spark draws (`graph.fail` keyed `(step_no << 20) | subject_id`, a 63-bit owner key, valid per the D.10 maintenance note), Sanity's `sanity.*` streams, and every persisted counter. They never read the epoch and replay exactly after any restore.
- **`restore_epoch` is stated here once** (IC-5). Save/Load owns it and persists it in `slot_epoch.bin` (ADR-0006). The kernel holds it in `kernel.clock` as a read-only, **non-persisted, non-hashed** value, set by `request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, …)` and `request_new_game(world_seed, restore_epoch)`; it is in no state block, in no canonical byte string, in no `state_hash` and in no snapshot header. The only simulation-visible use is inside `RngFacet.draw_epoch`.
- **Golden vectors** (reproduced on 4.7.2 and in the Python reference; `world_seed = 0x5EED000000002026`): `rng_derive(seed, "horror.tell", 17)` = `0xB2AA94991B52A02E` (`unit` 0.6979153513, `rng_int(600, 1800)` = 1438); counter 0 = `0x4988DBEFD7F20FF5`; `rng_derive(seed, "graph.failure", 0)` = `0x0CEEC43F97221B55`; with `world_seed = -1` (all ones), `("horror.tell", 1)` = `0x883EA97FED4A4613`; epoch 1 (`counter_eff` 1,048,593) = `0x6EFE2D9E722654C6`; epoch 2 (2,097,169) = `0xA46E009E591F2390`. Also `fnv64("horror.tell")` = `0xE500B5B58A7689E2`, `mix64(1)` = `0x5692161D100B05E5`, `mix64(0x8000000000000000)` = `0x25C26EA579CEA98A`. All values here and below print as numeric hex of the signed `int`'s bit pattern, most significant digit first.

**2.5 The one float path.** `unit` and `int_in` are the only floating-point expressions in the simulation. `lsr(raw, 11)` is below `2^53`, so the integer converts to `float` exactly and the division by `2^53` is exact; `unit * float(span)` is a single IEEE-754 binary64 multiplication, correctly rounded on every platform Godot supports, and `floori` is exact. There is no transcendental, no fused multiply-add opportunity in a single product, and no accumulated float. The only possible disagreement with an exact-integer evaluation is a product within `2^-53` relative of an integer boundary, a probability of about `span * 2^-53` per draw (below `2^-42` for the spans in use); that is the bias D.10 already states. The kernel GDD owns this formula and its goldens; this ADR does not replace it with an integer split (a 64-bit split overflows at spans near `2^32`, and a different rounding would silently change drawn values). The test oracle is an arbitrary-precision evaluation of `floor(top53 * span / 2^53)`; a mismatch there is reported to the technical-director as a candidate for an exact integer path, never fixed ad hoc.

**2.6 The shared pure-integer hash `Ihash`** (closes the "ADR candidate" in HE-42, AT-28, LO-19 and Instruments; PF D.14 is left to ADR-0024, open question 2). It is the form `he_hash` already defines, parameterised by a seed:

```
ihash(seed, k1, k2, k3, salt) = lsr( mix64( mix64(k1 ^ seed) ^ mix64(k2 ^ salt) ^ (k3 * GOLDEN) ), 1 )
```

The result is a **non-negative 63-bit `int`**, so every `mod` on it acts on a non-negative number. `Ihash.h32(...)` is `ihash(...) & 0xFFFFFFFF`. It is not a random stream: it has no counter and no state, it is never persisted, and it is used for variation that must be reproducible without being a persisted draw (Horror mark seeds, LURK waypoint rank and L3 timing with `HE_HASH_SEED` 0x4845; Attention beat jitter `h32(tell_epoch, k, 0, HASH_SEED)`; Lighting gutter onset `H(emitter_id, k)`; Instruments tremor from `ref_key`). Rules: callers pick a fixed non-zero seed or salt (`mix64(0) = 0` makes `ihash(0, 0, 0, 0, 0)` equal 0); inputs are stable ids and indices, never `tick_alpha`, `present_time` or a frame count; each system keeps its own seed constant so changing one re-rolls only that system. Presentation may call it (it is pure); it must never call `DetRng.derive`. Reference vectors (Python and GDScript agree): `ihash(0x4845, 1, 0, 0, 1)` = `0x2B1792AE18418A3E`; `ihash(0x4845, 17, 3, 5, 2)` = `0x31500F22473CCE18`; `ihash(0x4845, -1, -1, -1, 5)` = `0x0CA990E4614F7103`.

**2.7 Who uses what.**

| System | Draws | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Graph | thaw-burst (and spark ignition, VS-A) | plain stream `graph.fail`, counter `(step_no << 20) \| subject_id`, `subject_id < 2^20` asserted |
| Attention | tell length | epoch-keyed `attention.tell`, `draw_epoch`, then `int_in`; counter persisted; beat jitter by `Ihash` |
| Horror | REACH length | epoch-keyed `horror.tell`; marks, waypoints, L3 by `Ihash` |
| Sanity | lie, lure, phantom, hide | plain `sanity.<stream>/<PlayerId>[/<stable_id>]` via `dynamic_stream`; counters persisted; draw count fixed per outcome |
| Layout, Body, Assembly, Suit, Web Map, Boarding, Emitter, Interaction, Controller | none | `ModuleFacet.rng` is null |
| Lighting, Instruments, Perception Filter, Audio | presentation variation | `Ihash` (pure), never `DetRng.derive` |

### 3. Canonical encoding

**3.1 One encoder, no owner byte writers** (resolves the LS-21 / D.12 conflict and the framing half of OQ-8). Canonical bytes are produced only by `CanonicalEncoder.encode(value)` over the payload an owner's `snapshot(ctx)` delivers through `ctx.put(payload)`, or over a content value (ADR-0007 inputs). An owner's GDD describes the *shape* of its payload (keys, value types, row order) and never a byte layout. Consequently:
- The Graph publishes no `[u32 tag][u32 len][bytes]` writer. Its `snapshot` payload is a `Dictionary` whose values are named `PackedInt64Array` / `PackedInt32Array` / `PackedByteArray` fields (and the `def_off` / `def_utf8` pair), and the kernel encodes it. The "fixed documented order" of LS-21 is replaced by **sorted key order** (§ 3.3): renaming a payload key changes the hash and therefore needs a `schema_version` bump. The raw-bytes cost the Graph wanted is kept: a packed array reaches the buffer by one `to_byte_array()` copy (P14: 0.002 ms for 96 KB), with no per-element loop.
- `canonical_bytes()` and `block_hash()` on an owner (TR-lsg-021, TR-emitter-038, TR-debug-033) become kernel-side reads: `canonical_encode(snapshot payload)` and the kernel's `block_hash(block_id)` (§ 5). An owner that wants to expose "its hash" forwards to the kernel read; it computes nothing.
- The Item DB's `ItemInstance` "canonical positional encoding with canonical zeros" (TR-itemdb-012) is a **payload-shape rule**: an instance is an `Array` of `int`s in a fixed positional order, every non-applicable field present as the canonical zero, so a holder block has one encoding per state. The encoder then writes each as `INT`. The byte bound in TR-itemdb-029 (96 bytes per instance) was derived from `var_to_bytes(inst.to_array(), false)`, which is ADR-0002's size check and ADR-0006's storage form, not hash input; the TLV size of the same array is 9 bytes per int plus 9 for the array header (open question 6).

**3.2 The type set is closed.** One tag byte, then a self-delimiting body, so no encoding is a prefix of another and the map from normalised values to bytes is injective (D.12; KRN-HASH-01). All counts and lengths are **u64 little-endian**. Integers are 8-byte little-endian two's complement.

| Tag | Type | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `0x00` | NIL | none |
| `0x01` | BOOL | 1 byte, 0 or 1 |
| `0x02` | INT | 8 bytes, little-endian two's complement |
| `0x03` | FLOAT | 8 bytes, IEEE-754 binary64 bits, little-endian, after normalisation (§ 3.4) |
| `0x04` | STRING | u64 UTF-8 byte length, then the bytes; **a `StringName` encodes as the `STRING` of its text** |
| `0x05` | VECTOR2 | two normalised FLOAT bodies (16 bytes, no inner tags); components widen from `float32` to binary64 |
| `0x06` | VECTOR2I | two 8-byte little-endian ints (16 bytes, no inner tags) |
| `0x07` | ARRAY | u64 element count, then that many tagged values in order. Typed and untyped arrays encode identically. |
| `0x08` | DICT | u64 entry count, then `key, value` tagged pairs sorted by key (§ 3.3). Typed and untyped dictionaries encode identically. |
| `0x09` | PACKED | 1 element-type byte, u64 element count, then the elements as raw little-endian bytes |

Packed element-type bytes: `1` `PackedByteArray` (1 byte per element), `2` `PackedInt32Array` (4), `3` `PackedInt64Array` (8), `4` `PackedFloat32Array` (4), `5` `PackedFloat64Array` (8), `6` `PackedStringArray` (each element a u64 length plus UTF-8), `7` `PackedVector2Array` (two 4-byte floats per element). Any other `Variant` type (an `Object`, `Callable`, `Signal`, `RID`, `Color`, `Rect2i`, `Vector3`, a packed array not listed) is `ENC_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE`. Adding a tag or a packed type changes the hash definition and needs a new `hash_algo` (§ 4.4). `bool` is never confused with `int`: they have separate tags.

**3.3 Dictionary key order** (resolves the key-order half of OQ-8; this deliberately replaces D.12's "sorted bytewise by the encoded key bytes"). A dictionary's keys are all `int` or all of the string family (`String` / `StringName`); a mixture is `ENC_MIXED_KEYS`, and any other key type is `ENC_KEY_TYPE` (CR-4 already requires one key type). The encoder sorts:
- **`int` keys** ascending by signed numeric value (`-5, 3, 10`).
- **String-family keys** ascending by code point of `String(key)`, which equals UTF-8 byte order (P12). `StringName` keys are converted to `String` before the sort; the `StringName` comparison is never used.
- After sorting, two keys that are equal as text (a `StringName(&"a")` and a `String("a")` both present) are `ENC_DUP_KEY`.

The reason for the change: the bytewise order of the *encoded* integer key puts `3, 10` before `-5` and orders strings by length first, because the encoded key begins with a little-endian length. That order is deterministic but meaningless, and the diff the G4 test prints ("the first differing `block_id` and key") reads naturally only in value order. Value order is also what `Array.sort()` gives with no custom comparator, so the encoder needs no byte-comparison helper (GDScript cannot order two `PackedByteArray`s). Both orders are equally injective, so the change costs nothing in collision safety and no hash exists yet. `gdd_sync` item for the kernel GDD D.12 and KRN-HASH-01.

**3.4 Normalisation.** `FLOAT` and the components of `VECTOR2`: `f != f` (any NaN, whatever its payload) encodes as the bits `0x7FF8000000000000`; `f == 0.0` (both zeros) encodes as `0x0000000000000000`; everything else as its binary64 bits. These need explicit branches because `encode_double` preserves NaN payloads and the sign of zero (P11). `PackedFloat32Array`, `PackedFloat64Array` and `PackedVector2Array` are **not** normalised by the encoder: they reach the buffer as raw bytes, and a NaN payload or a negative zero inside one survives (P11). Therefore owners keep NaN and `-0.0` out of packed float state (their mutators normalise), and in strict mode (§ 3.5) the encoder scans every packed float array for a NaN or a negative-zero bit pattern and fails with `ENC_FLOAT_NONCANONICAL`. Floats in SIM blocks are in any case outside the contract (§ 1.2); this rule only makes the exception safe.

**3.5 Errors and strict mode.** `encode` returns a `PackedByteArray` and sets `error` (an `ENC_*` code) and `error_path` (a short text path such as `bodies/2/pos`, built only when an error occurs, never on the success path). On error the returned array is empty and the caller treats the block as unhashable: `block_hash` returns `ok = false` with `BLOCK_HASH_ENCODE_ERROR`; inside a capture it is the existing `CAPTURE_ERROR` fault (ADR-0003 domain 0, code 7) with `error` and `error_path` in the detail. No new domain-0 fault code is added by this ADR. Codes: `ENC_OK` 0, `ENC_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE` 1, `ENC_MIXED_KEYS` 2, `ENC_KEY_TYPE` 3, `ENC_DUP_KEY` 4, `ENC_DEPTH` 5 (nesting deeper than `ENC_MAX_DEPTH` 16, which also stops a cyclic container), `ENC_SIZE` 6 (output above `ENC_MAX_BYTES`, default 16 MiB, never below Save/Load's `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES`), `ENC_FLOAT_IN_BLOCK` 7 (strict only), `ENC_FLOAT_NONCANONICAL` 8 (strict only). **Strict mode** is on in tests and `STRICT_DEBUG` builds and for content hashes (`Hash64.of_value`); it additionally rejects any `FLOAT` / `VECTOR2` / packed float in a block not on the float allow-list (§ 1.2). Release builds run the non-strict encoder on the capture and K-4 paths: correctness there rests on the owners' mutators and the tests, and a payload float would still encode canonically (normalised) rather than silently.

**3.6 Shape rules for payloads** (so the encoder stays cheap). A block of more than about 250 scalar fields snapshots as packed arrays, not nested dictionaries (D.11's per-block budget). Payload dictionaries use `StringName` or `String` keys (or `int` keys for per-id tables), never both. Derived caches, diagnostics counters (`graph_*`, `hash_invocations`, `horror.view.debug`) and anything marked non-persisted are not in the payload and never in a hash (TR-lsg-039, TR-horror-020). Entity references are stable ids, never array positions of a different block. The encoder walks the payload once; it allocates one scratch `PackedByteArray` that it reuses across calls, one `keys()` array per dictionary node, and the final exactly-sized result; that allocation belongs to the dirty path and is bounded by the number of dirty blocks (S0-e measures it).

**3.7 Worked vectors** (hand-derived for the first four from D.12, produced by the GDScript probe, and reproduced by the independent Python implementation; `u64(n)` is 8 little-endian bytes; the `H64` column is the numeric value of the first 8 digest bytes read little-endian).

| Value | Canonical bytes | `H64` |
|---|---|---|
| `INT 1` | `02 u64(1)` | `0xA8514B868B9B6F67` |
| `FLOAT 1.0` | `03 00 00 00 00 00 00 F0 3F` | `0xF9257072CFA72232` |
| `[[1],[2,3]]` | `07 u64(2) 07 u64(1) 02 u64(1) 07 u64(2) 02 u64(2) 02 u64(3)` | `0xE5C1840AAE2E4EC0` |
| `[[1,2],[3]]` | `07 u64(2) 07 u64(2) 02 u64(1) 02 u64(2) 07 u64(1) 02 u64(3)` | `0xA09749F81F3D6976` |
| `&"a"` and `"a"` | `04 u64(1) 61` (equal) | `0x33A10EBD15E04FB8` |
| `{"b": 1, "a": 2}` and `{"a": 2, "b": 1}` | `08 u64(2) 04 u64(1) 61 02 u64(2) 04 u64(1) 62 02 u64(1)` (equal) | `0xE39AE16B84B9F022` |
| `{10: 1, -5: 2, 3: 3}` | `08 u64(3) 02 s64(-5) 02 u64(2) 02 u64(3) 02 u64(3) 02 u64(10) 02 u64(1)` | `0x3994B5446692B06D` |
| `PackedInt32Array([1, -2])` | `09 02 u64(2) 01 00 00 00 FE FF FF FF` | `0xA02103D5B9B9D438` |
| `Vector2(-0.0, 1.0)` | `05 00×8 00 00 00 00 00 00 F0 3F` | `0x3B288246B7BCE33A` |
| `Vector2i(-1, 2)` | `06 FF×8 u64(2)` | `0xBA1BD293E871B0D2` |
| `null` / `true` | `00` / `01 01` | `0x987AB3FF9C0B346E` / `0x2326F384A197CF9D` |

The two nested arrays differ at the second count, so they cannot collide; `INT 1` and `FLOAT 1.0` differ at the tag. A property test over 10,000 seeded random values asserts `encode(a) == encode(b)` only when `a` and `b` are equal after normalisation (KRN-HASH-01).

### 4. `H64`, `block_hash` and `state_hash`

**4.1 `H64`.** `H64(bytes)` is the first 8 bytes of `SHA-256(bytes)`, read as a little-endian two's-complement `int` (`digest.decode_s64(0)`, P13). It is computed by `HashingContext` (native; P14: 0.33 ms for 150 KB on the dev machine), through one reusable context held by the kernel's `StateHasher` (`start` / `update` / `finish`, P13). `hash_algo` = **2** names it (SL-16); ids 0 (xxHash64) and 1 (FNV-1a 64) are reserved and not written. **A scripted per-byte 64-bit hash is banned** for state hashing (D.11, TR-section-032): it would be 15 to 150 ms over 90 KiB by SL's estimate (UNVERIFIED) against 0.33 ms for the native path, and the built-in `hash()` is not a stable cross-version contract. Reference: `H64("abc")` is `0xEACF018FBF1678BA`.

**4.2 Two representations, never mixed.** The numeric `int` of a hash prints (for logs and the Overlay) as `0x` plus 16 hex digits **most significant first**. The `hex64` string used in headers and JSON (S-1, SL F-10) is the **8 little-endian bytes** of the same `int` as 16 lowercase hex characters, which for an `H64` is exactly the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 digest. So `H64("abc")` is numeric `0xEACF018FBF1678BA` and `hex64` `"ba7816bf8f01cfea"`; `world_seed = -1` is `"ffffffffffffffff"`; `2^53 + 1` is `"0100000000002000"`; `2^63` (the `int` `-9223372036854775808`) is `"0000000000000080"`. `Hex64.encode(x)` builds the string from `encode_s64` and `hex_encode()`; `Hex64.decode(s)` first validates exactly 16 characters of `[0-9a-f]` (P16: `hex_decode` alone accepts uppercase and mis-reports errors) and then `decode_s64`; neither uses `String.hex_to_int` or a general integer parse.

**4.3 `block_hash`.** `block_hash(b) = H64(canonical_encode(snapshot payload of b))` with no framing, so it equals the value Save/Load stores as `block_state_hash` (SL-16) and the value Layout reads as `layout_hash()`.

**4.4 `state_hash`** (resolves the fold half of OQ-8). Every length, count and scalar in the fold is a **u64 little-endian** (8 bytes), except `block_hash`, which is the 8 digest bytes as `H64` produced them (equivalently `encode_s64` of the `int`). The fold is hashed as a stream, never built as one big array:

```
state_hash(scope, T, uncached) = H64( s64(T) || s64(world_seed) || record(b1) || record(b2) || ... )     blocks sorted ascending by block_id
record(b) = u64(len(block_id)) || utf8(block_id) || u64(schema_version) || u64(len(canonical_bytes(b))) || s64(block_hash(b))
```

`block_id` order is ascending code point of `String(block_id)` (P12); `len(block_id)` is its UTF-8 byte length. An empty scope hashes `s64(T) || s64(world_seed)`. Because every variable-length part is length-prefixed and every other part is fixed width, the concatenation is injective. `restore_epoch` is not an input (§ 2.4), and neither is `correlation`, a diagnostics counter, or the command log. **Scopes** (D.12): `PERSIST` = blocks with `persist = true` **and** `persist_scope = WORLD`; `ALL_SIM` = every `SIM` block (WORLD, PROFILE and non-persisted derived); both exclude `kernel.clock` (its `T` and `world_seed` are the prefix, counted once) and never include `PERCEPTION_OUT`. `hash_algo` 2 names **the whole definition in this section and § 3**: the tag set, the key order, the normalisation, the fold framing and the digest truncation. Any change to any of them is a new `hash_algo` value, not a silent edit; a save with an unsupported `hash_algo` loads REBASED (SL-12) rather than comparing.

**4.5 Worked fold** (probed and reproduced in Python): `T = 5000`, `world_seed = 0x5EED000000002026`, block `a.state` (`schema_version` 1, payload `{"x": 1}`: bytes `08 u64(1) 04 u64(1) 78 02 u64(1)`, 26 bytes, `block_hash` `0x85A68464E47356C1`) and block `b.state` (`schema_version` 2, payload `[1, 2]`: bytes `07 u64(2) 02 u64(1) 02 u64(2)`, 27 bytes, `block_hash` `0xF1B6635FE3BC2290`). The fold input is 16 + (8 + 7 + 8 + 8 + 8) + (8 + 7 + 8 + 8 + 8) = 94 bytes, and `state_hash(PERSIST, 5000)` = **`0x81AB3842EF1E8DEF`**. These, plus the `"abc"` vector and the § 2.4 vectors, are the frozen goldens of KRN-HASH-01..03; the Ship Body 518-byte fixture is added when the reference encoder confirms or corrects its length.

**4.6 Content hashes** (inputs fixed by ADR-0007 § 3.4 and § 3.5). `Hash64.of_value(value)` = `H64(CanonicalEncoder.encode(value, strict = true))`. `catalogue_hash` = `of_value(rows)` where `rows` is an `Array` of per-def `Array`s of post-cast integers and `def_id` strings, sorted ascending by `def_id` in code-point order (equal to the byte order ADR-0007 requires). `template_hash`, `geometry_hash`, `visual_hash` = `of_value` of the post-cast template payload (or the geometry / visual sub-payload, whose shape is Layout's and ADR-0013's), computed once at load. Layout stores the `u32` form `Hash64.low32(h)` in a `PackedInt32Array` and compares only after `& 0xFFFFFFFF` (P9, TR-section-032). Content hashes are diagnostic and never gate a load (ADR-0007 § 3.4). Their golden vectors are committed after this ADR is Accepted (ADR-0007 Validation).

**4.7 What the kernel hashes and when.** No hash runs in P2 or P3, and none runs on a tick where no consumer asks (§ 5.4). The consumers are: the Overlay cadence (`DIAG_HASH_CADENCE_TICKS` 60, outside P3, cached profile); `layout_hash()` and Horror's path cache (`block_hash` read from P3 onward or a boundary, memoised by the caller on its own mutation counter); the snapshot capture (`SAVING`, uncached, one `snapshot` per block whose payload feeds both the canonical encode and Save/Load's `var_to_bytes`); the K-4 reproduction compare after `post_restore` (uncached); the `STRICT_DEBUG` tripwire (D.12, at most two whole-set uncached hashes per dispatch batch plus one around P5); and the tests.

**4.8 64-bit interchange** (TR-cmd-038, shared with ADR-0006). A value that can exceed `2^53` (`T`, `world_seed`, `state_hash`, every block hash, `campaign_id`) crosses a JSON boundary only as `hex64`; a `Marshalls.raw_to_base64` string is allowed for opaque byte blobs. A snapshot's in-memory round trip through `var_to_bytes` / `bytes_to_var` is lossless for `int64` (the binary form carries 8 bytes), and that is Save/Load's storage form; it is never hash input (registry `payload_size_check`). The Web Map's 8-byte seeds are `PackedByteArray` bytes in their block and so need no integer treatment (WM-37).

### 5. Cached block hashes (K-1)

**5.1 What is cached.** The kernel holds, per registered block, `{hash: int, enc_len: int, valid: bool}` in three parallel packed arrays sized once at the registry freeze: `PackedInt64Array` hashes, `PackedInt64Array` lengths, `PackedByteArray` valid flags. It lives in the kernel's registries group (ADR-0003 § 10, H1), counters in its diagnostics group. The cache stores the length too, so `state_hash` can fold a cached block without re-encoding it.

**5.2 Invalidation.** `valid[b] = 0` is set by the kernel's single block-written entry point, which `WriteScope.mark_dirty` (ADR-0003 § 4, ADR-0004) calls for any key, and by `restore`, `init_world` and `default_state` for the block they replace. It is invalidated **only** by those, never by a property setter (4.7: a packed-array element write skips the setter, P8) and never by `open_for` alone (a mutator that opens a scope and changes nothing leaves the cache valid, which keeps a quiet tick at zero encodes). A mutator that writes and forgets `mark_dirty` leaves a stale cache; that is exactly the bug the uncached verification paths exist to catch (KRN-HASH-02).

**5.3 Reads.** `block_hash(block_id, uncached = true) -> BlockHashResult` (D.12) is available in every build. It is a pure read: the kernel calls the owner's `snapshot` with a dedicated `SnapshotContext` of its own, encodes, hashes, and mutates no block. Order of checks: (1) unknown id or a non-`persist` block: `ok = false`, `BLOCK_HASH_UNKNOWN`, never a hash of 0; (2) the active `WriteScope` has opened the block (`scope.has_opened(block_index)`, true from the first `open_for` of that block until the scope is re-armed): `ok = false`, `BLOCK_HASH_IN_WRITE`; (3) `uncached = false` and `valid`: return the cache; (4) otherwise `snapshot`, encode, `H64`, set `ok`; an encoder error gives `BLOCK_HASH_ENCODE_ERROR`. Only a **cached** read stores into the cache (and counts one encode if it had to compute); an **uncached** read ignores the cache, writes nothing, and counts exactly one `canonical_bytes` encode. A hook that has written Layout and then reads `layout_hash()` inside the same hook therefore gets `BLOCK_HASH_IN_WRITE`: read it from another hook or a boundary, or after the writing hook returns. `snapshot` is not re-entrant (ADR-0003), so `block_hash` called from inside a `snapshot` is a defect that the re-entrancy flag reports as `CTX_REENTRANT`.

**5.4 Which path uses the cache.** Only the **diagnostics cadence** (the Overlay's `state_hash` display, the Overlay's HASH_DRIFT block naming) and a caller memoising its own reads may use `uncached = false`. **Every determinism check uses `uncached = true`**: G3, G4, the K-4 window, the cross-process test, the `STRICT_DEBUG` tripwire, the snapshot capture, the weld property test and the golden comparisons. The reason is the same as D.12's: a cached comparison would pass falsely on the missed-dirty-mark bug.

**5.5 Stale-cache detector (hash side of ADR-0004's debug check).** In `STRICT_DEBUG` and test builds, each diagnostics-cadence refresh recomputes `uncached` for every block whose cache is `valid` and, if the two differ, counts `HASH_CACHE_STALE`, reports it as a violation naming the block, and invalidates the entry. This finds a forgotten `mark_dirty` within one cadence, independently of ADR-0004's per-key check; it costs one extra encode per valid block per cadence in debug only. Release builds do not run it.

**5.6 Cost accounting.** Counters (diagnostics, never hashed, reset at BOOTING and at restore): `enc_blocks` (encodes performed), `enc_bytes`, `enc_elem_loops` (element-loop iterations over non-packed scalars), `hash_calls`, `cache_hits`, `HASH_CACHE_STALE`. KRN-PERF-01: a quiet tick with no dirty block and no reader shows `enc_blocks` = 0. KRN-PERF-02: a cached-profile read after a tick that dirtied `k` blocks shows `enc_blocks` = `k` (the blocks invalidated since the previous cached read). KRN-PERF-05: packed arrays reach the buffer by `to_byte_array()` and contribute 0 to `enc_elem_loops`. `HashingContext` over 150 KB must stay at or below 1 ms on RM-DECK (TR-lsg-037, S0-d); if a release-export measurement exceeds it, the ladder is: keep the cache (already), then hash on the Save/Load worker from the encoded bytes (the worker may call `HashingContext`), then split large packed arrays into per-section sub-payloads whose hashes fold, with a new `hash_algo`.

### 6. Verification and replay tests

The determinism claims are tested, not asserted (TD-FEASIBILITY: "determinism claimed, not tested"):
- **G3:** two independent kernels, the fixture blocks of the Determinism acceptance criteria, `world_seed` fixed, a recorded 1,000-tick stream: `state_hash(ALL_SIM, 1000, uncached = true)` equal; plus the cross-process variant through `OS.execute` with `(save bytes, restore_epoch)` passed on the command line.
- **G4:** snapshot at `T = 500` at a boundary with no `PLAYER` command pending, restore with the same pinned epoch, continue to 1,100: `state_hash(PERSIST, 1100)` equal to the control; on a mismatch the diff names the first differing `block_id` and key over the uncached TLV bytes.
- **Render-rate independence:** the same 10-second scripted replay at `max_fps` 30, 60, 144 and 0 gives the same hash (TR-pxl-022, ADR-0001).
- **Encoder:** KRN-HASH-01 property test (injectivity under normalisation), the § 3.7 vectors, the § 4.5 fold, KRN-HASH-03 (`block_hash` read semantics and counters), and the strict-mode rejection tests for each `ENC_*` code.
- **RNG:** the § 2.4 vectors, the epoch triple (KRN-EPO-01: the three epoch values differ), a facet misuse test (`draw` on an epoch-keyed stream), a stream-registration collision test, and a 1,000,000-draw comparison of `int_in` against the arbitrary-precision oracle.
- **Cross-OS golden files** (`tests/golden/`, TR-lsg-031): `graph_state_hash_f_mvp_healthy.txt`, `graph_state_hash_weld_cut.txt` and the thaw-roll draw sequence, generated once on the first passing build and compared on Windows, Linux and macOS runners.
- **Lints:** the § 1.7 table, each rule with a committed bad and good fixture file.

### Implementation Guidelines

- **Must** write every simulation quantity as an `int`; **must never** declare a `float` in `src/sim/**` or store one in a persisted SIM block, except on the committed allow-list.
- **Must** write every 64-bit constant as a signed decimal `int` literal; **must never** write a hexadecimal literal above `0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`, and **must never** shift a negative literal.
- **Must** use `IntMath.lsr` for any right shift of a possibly negative value; **must never** call it with `n` outside `1..63`.
- **Must** divide and take modulus through `IntMath.floor_div` / `ceil_div` / `posmod_i`, or use a bare `/` or `%` only with `@warning_ignore("integer_division")` (for `/`) and a `# nn:` comment naming why both operands are non-negative; **must never** rely on truncation toward zero for a quotient meant as a floor.
- **Must** keep every sim intermediate below `2^62` in magnitude and check declared factor maxima at boot; **must never** rely on integer wrap outside `mix64`, `fnv64`, `Ihash` and the fold.
- **Must** iterate dense arrays in ascending id order, and extract and sort `Dictionary` keys before iterating one; **must never** iterate an unsorted `Dictionary`, sort `StringName`s, use `sort_custom` or any sort over tie-able keys, or call `hash()`, `get_instance_id()`, `shuffle()` or `pick_random()`.
- **Must** draw randomness only through `ModuleFacet.rng`, with one registered stream per independent sequence and its counter inside the owner's persisted block; **must never** call `randi`, `randf`, `RandomNumberGenerator` or any global generator, and **must never** register a stream on a module whose GDD says it draws nothing.
- **Must** call `draw_epoch` for `attention.tell` and `horror.tell` and `draw` for every other stream; **must never** compute `rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE * restore_epoch` outside `RngFacet`, store `restore_epoch` in a block, or hash it.
- **Must** compute a stream's key once at registration; **must never** call `fnv64` or `stream_key` on a draw path.
- **Must** use `Ihash` for presentation variation and non-RNG sim variation, with a fixed non-zero seed per system; **must never** feed it `tick_alpha`, `present_time` or a frame count, and **must never** call `DetRng.derive` from presentation.
- **Must** deliver a state block's canonical state through `snapshot(ctx)` as a plain `Dictionary` / `Array` / packed-array payload and let the kernel encode it; **must never** write an owner-side byte layout, call `encode_s64` / `encode_double` / `to_byte_array` for hashing, or feed `var_to_bytes` output to a hash.
- **Must** keep NaN and `-0.0` out of packed float arrays; **must never** put an `Object`, `Callable`, `RID` or `Color` in a snapshot payload.
- **Must** compute every hash through `HashingContext` (`StateHasher`, `Hash64`); **must never** write a scripted per-byte hash or use the built-in `hash()` for state.
- **Must** mark dirty through `scope.mark_dirty` after any write to a block, including a packed-array element write; **must never** rely on a setter to invalidate the hash cache.
- **Must** call `block_hash(id)` and `state_hash` with `uncached = true` on every determinism check, capture, K-4 compare and test; **must never** use `uncached = false` for anything but diagnostics display and a caller's own memoised read.
- **Must** read `block_hash` from P3 onward (from a hook that did not write that block) or from a boundary; **must never** read it inside an `apply` or from a hook after that hook has opened the block.
- **Must** print a hash for people as `0x` plus 16 hex digits most significant first and serialise it as `hex64`; **must never** write a 64-bit value as a JSON number or parse hex with `String.hex_to_int`.
- **Must** treat a change to the tag set, key order, normalisation, fold framing or digest truncation as a new `hash_algo`; **must** bump a block's `schema_version` when its payload shape changes; **must never** edit the definition in place.
- **Must** regenerate golden files only through the reviewed golden-update job, recording the commit; **must never** hand-edit a golden value.

### 3. Canonical encoding

**3.1 One encoder, no owner byte writers** (resolves the LS-21 / D.12 conflict and the framing half of OQ-8). Canonical bytes are produced only by `CanonicalEncoder.encode(value)` over the payload an owner's `snapshot(ctx)` delivers through `ctx.put(payload)`, or over a content value (ADR-0007 inputs). An owner's GDD describes the *shape* of its payload (keys, value types, row order) and never a byte layout. Consequently:
- The Graph publishes no `[u32 tag][u32 len][bytes]` writer. Its `snapshot` payload is a `Dictionary` whose values are named `PackedInt64Array` / `PackedInt32Array` / `PackedByteArray` fields (and the `def_off` / `def_utf8` pair), and the kernel encodes it. The "fixed documented order" of LS-21 is replaced by **sorted key order** (§ 3.3): renaming a payload key changes the hash and therefore needs a `schema_version` bump. The raw-bytes cost the Graph wanted is kept: a packed array reaches the buffer by one `to_byte_array()` copy (P14: 0.002 ms for 96 KB), with no per-element loop.
- `canonical_bytes()` and `block_hash()` on an owner (TR-lsg-021, TR-emitter-038, TR-debug-033) become kernel-side reads: `canonical_encode(snapshot payload)` and the kernel's `block_hash(block_id)` (§ 5). An owner that wants to expose "its hash" forwards to the kernel read; it computes nothing.
- The Item DB's `ItemInstance` "canonical positional encoding with canonical zeros" (TR-itemdb-012) is a **payload-shape rule**: an instance is an `Array` of `int`s in a fixed positional order, every non-applicable field present as the canonical zero, so a holder block has one encoding per state. The encoder then writes each as `INT`. The byte bound in TR-itemdb-029 (96 bytes per instance) was derived from `var_to_bytes(inst.to_array(), false)`, which is ADR-0002's size check and ADR-0006's storage form, not hash input; the TLV size of the same array is 9 bytes per int plus 9 for the array header (open question 6).

**3.2 The type set is closed.** One tag byte, then a self-delimiting body, so no encoding is a prefix of another and the map from normalised values to bytes is injective (D.12; KRN-HASH-01). All counts and lengths are **u64 little-endian**. Integers are 8-byte little-endian two's complement.

| Tag | Type | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `0x00` | NIL | none |
| `0x01` | BOOL | 1 byte, 0 or 1 |
| `0x02` | INT | 8 bytes, little-endian two's complement |
| `0x03` | FLOAT | 8 bytes, IEEE-754 binary64 bits, little-endian, after normalisation (§ 3.4) |
| `0x04` | STRING | u64 UTF-8 byte length, then the bytes; **a `StringName` encodes as the `STRING` of its text** |
| `0x05` | VECTOR2 | two normalised FLOAT bodies (16 bytes, no inner tags); components widen from `float32` to binary64 |
| `0x06` | VECTOR2I | two 8-byte little-endian ints (16 bytes, no inner tags) |
| `0x07` | ARRAY | u64 element count, then that many tagged values in order. Typed and untyped arrays encode identically. |
| `0x08` | DICT | u64 entry count, then `key, value` tagged pairs sorted by key (§ 3.3). Typed and untyped dictionaries encode identically. |
| `0x09` | PACKED | 1 element-type byte, u64 element count, then the elements as raw little-endian bytes |

Packed element-type bytes: `1` `PackedByteArray` (1 byte per element), `2` `PackedInt32Array` (4), `3` `PackedInt64Array` (8), `4` `PackedFloat32Array` (4), `5` `PackedFloat64Array` (8), `6` `PackedStringArray` (each element a u64 length plus UTF-8), `7` `PackedVector2Array` (two 4-byte floats per element). Any other `Variant` type (an `Object`, `Callable`, `Signal`, `RID`, `Color`, `Rect2i`, `Vector3`, a packed array not listed) is `ENC_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE`. Adding a tag or a packed type changes the hash definition and needs a new `hash_algo` (§ 4.4). `bool` is never confused with `int`: they have separate tags.

**3.3 Dictionary key order** (resolves the key-order half of OQ-8; this deliberately replaces D.12's "sorted bytewise by the encoded key bytes"). A dictionary's keys are all `int` or all of the string family (`String` / `StringName`); a mixture is `ENC_MIXED_KEYS`, and any other key type is `ENC_KEY_TYPE` (CR-4 already requires one key type). The encoder sorts:
- **`int` keys** ascending by signed numeric value (`-5, 3, 10`).
- **String-family keys** ascending by code point of `String(key)`, which equals UTF-8 byte order (P12). `StringName` keys are converted to `String` before the sort; the `StringName` comparison is never used.
- After sorting, two keys that are equal as text (a `StringName(&"a")` and a `String("a")` both present) are `ENC_DUP_KEY`.

The reason for the change: the bytewise order of the *encoded* integer key puts `3, 10` before `-5` and orders strings by length first, because the encoded key begins with a little-endian length. That order is deterministic but meaningless, and the diff the G4 test prints ("the first differing `block_id` and key") reads naturally only in value order. Value order is also what `Array.sort()` gives with no custom comparator, so the encoder needs no byte-comparison helper (GDScript cannot order two `PackedByteArray`s). Both orders are equally injective, so the change costs nothing in collision safety and no hash exists yet. `gdd_sync` item for the kernel GDD D.12 and KRN-HASH-01.

**3.4 Normalisation.** `FLOAT` and the components of `VECTOR2`: `f != f` (any NaN, whatever its payload) encodes as the bits `0x7FF8000000000000`; `f == 0.0` (both zeros) encodes as `0x0000000000000000`; everything else as its binary64 bits. These need explicit branches because `encode_double` preserves NaN payloads and the sign of zero (P11). `PackedFloat32Array`, `PackedFloat64Array` and `PackedVector2Array` are **not** normalised by the encoder: they reach the buffer as raw bytes, and a NaN payload or a negative zero inside one survives (P11). Therefore owners keep NaN and `-0.0` out of packed float state (their mutators normalise), and in strict mode (§ 3.5) the encoder scans every packed float array for a NaN or a negative-zero bit pattern and fails with `ENC_FLOAT_NONCANONICAL`. Floats in SIM blocks are in any case outside the contract (§ 1.2); this rule only makes the exception safe.

**3.5 Errors and strict mode.** `encode` returns a `PackedByteArray` and sets `error` (an `ENC_*` code) and `error_path` (a short text path such as `bodies/2/pos`, built only when an error occurs, never on the success path). On error the returned array is empty and the caller treats the block as unhashable: `block_hash` returns `ok = false` with `BLOCK_HASH_ENCODE_ERROR`; inside a capture it is the existing `CAPTURE_ERROR` fault (ADR-0003 domain 0, code 7) with `error` and `error_path` in the detail. No new domain-0 fault code is added by this ADR. Codes: `ENC_OK` 0, `ENC_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE` 1, `ENC_MIXED_KEYS` 2, `ENC_KEY_TYPE` 3, `ENC_DUP_KEY` 4, `ENC_DEPTH` 5 (nesting deeper than `ENC_MAX_DEPTH` 16, which also stops a cyclic container), `ENC_SIZE` 6 (output above `ENC_MAX_BYTES`, default 16 MiB, never below Save/Load's `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES`), `ENC_FLOAT_IN_BLOCK` 7 (strict only), `ENC_FLOAT_NONCANONICAL` 8 (strict only). **Strict mode** is on in tests and `STRICT_DEBUG` builds and for content hashes (`Hash64.of_value`); it additionally rejects any `FLOAT` / `VECTOR2` / packed float in a block not on the float allow-list (§ 1.2). Release builds run the non-strict encoder on the capture and K-4 paths: correctness there rests on the owners' mutators and the tests, and a payload float would still encode canonically (normalised) rather than silently.

**3.6 Shape rules for payloads** (so the encoder stays cheap). A block of more than about 250 scalar fields snapshots as packed arrays, not nested dictionaries (D.11's per-block budget). Payload dictionaries use `StringName` or `String` keys (or `int` keys for per-id tables), never both. Derived caches, diagnostics counters (`graph_*`, `hash_invocations`, `horror.view.debug`) and anything marked non-persisted are not in the payload and never in a hash (TR-lsg-039, TR-horror-020). Entity references are stable ids, never array positions of a different block. The encoder walks the payload once; it allocates one scratch `PackedByteArray` that it reuses across calls, one `keys()` array per dictionary node, and the final exactly-sized result; that allocation belongs to the dirty path and is bounded by the number of dirty blocks (S0-e measures it).

**3.7 Worked vectors** (hand-derived for the first four from D.12, produced by the GDScript probe, and reproduced by the independent Python implementation; `u64(n)` is 8 little-endian bytes; the `H64` column is the numeric value of the first 8 digest bytes read little-endian).

| Value | Canonical bytes | `H64` |
|---|---|---|
| `INT 1` | `02 u64(1)` | `0xA8514B868B9B6F67` |
| `FLOAT 1.0` | `03 00 00 00 00 00 00 F0 3F` | `0xF9257072CFA72232` |
| `[[1],[2,3]]` | `07 u64(2) 07 u64(1) 02 u64(1) 07 u64(2) 02 u64(2) 02 u64(3)` | `0xE5C1840AAE2E4EC0` |
| `[[1,2],[3]]` | `07 u64(2) 07 u64(2) 02 u64(1) 02 u64(2) 07 u64(1) 02 u64(3)` | `0xA09749F81F3D6976` |
